jobDescription: As an Identity & AI Security Specialist, you will strengthen HDB’s identity security capabilities and enable the secure adoption of Generative AI and agentic AI. Working with system owners, architects, operations teams, governance functions and partners, you will design, implement, administer and operate security controls and the supporting infrastructure for human identities, privileged accounts, service and workload identities, application credentials and AI agents across on-premises, cloud and AI-enabled environments. You will also help maintain the security, availability, performance and resilience of enterprise identity and AI security platforms and their underlying infrastructure.
jobResponsibilities:
• Shape identity and AI security: Review and improve policies, standards, reference architectures and control requirements in line with the threat landscape, regulatory obligations and industry practices.

  • Assess and reduce risk: Identify gaps affecting human, privileged, machine and AI identities; conduct security risk assessments; and recommend practical remediation measures and security solutions.

  • Engineer identity controls: Design, implement and enhance IAM, IGA, PAM, PIM, MFA, SSO, Conditional Access, RBAC, just-in-time access and access-governance capabilities across hybrid environments.

  • Govern the identity lifecycle: Establish controls for privileged accounts, service accounts, application identities, API credentials, workload identities and AI agents, including discovery, onboarding, recertification, credential rotation and decommissioning.

  • Secure AI use cases: Review Generative AI and agentic AI solutions and define controls for agent authentication and authorisation, tool and data access, secrets, prompt injection, excessive agency, data leakage, human approval, logging and auditability.

  • Maintain identity and AI security infrastructure: Administer, operate and maintain enterprise identity and AI security platforms and their underlying infrastructure. Monitor system health, capacity, availability, performance, security and integration dependencies; perform patching, upgrades, hardening, backup and recovery activities; troubleshoot technical issues; and coordinate maintenance and technology refreshes with internal teams and vendors.

  • Deliver secure and resilient solutions: Translate business, infrastructure and security requirements into solution designs and implementation plans; coordinate configuration, integration, testing, deployment and operational handover; and manage lifecycle upgrades, capacity needs, resilience and technology refresh activities.

  • Automate and integrate: Develop scripts, API integrations and workflows to improve identity discovery, provisioning, access reviews, credential management, monitoring and remediation.

  • Operate and respond: Monitor the health, availability, performance and security posture of identity and AI security platforms and their supporting infrastructure. Investigate alerts, service disruptions and security incidents; perform root-cause analysis; and implement timely recovery, containment, remediation and preventive measures.

  • Support assurance: Maintain technical documentation, operating procedures and control evidence; support audits and assessments; and ensure excessive, dormant or unauthorised access is remediated promptly.

  • Communicate outcomes: Analyse risks, trends and control effectiveness, and present clear recommendations and management reports to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
• Have a degree in cybersecurity, computer science, information systems, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

  • Have at least 3 years of relevant experience in identity security, cybersecurity engineering, infrastructure operations or security architecture, including hands-on experience implementing, administering or supporting enterprise identity and AI security platforms and their underlying infrastructure.

  • Have practical knowledge of enterprise infrastructure operations, including Windows Server or Linux administration, platform monitoring, system hardening, patching, backup and recovery, high availability, capacity management, change management and technical troubleshooting.

  • Understand identity lifecycle management, authentication, authorisation, Zero Trust, least privilege, segregation of duties, privileged access, access reviews and identity-related threat scenarios.

  • Have working knowledge of enterprise identity technologies and integration patterns, including Active Directory or Microsoft Entra ID, SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SCIM, LDAP, Kerberos, federation and REST APIs.

  • Can analyse complex security and operational issues, translate requirements into practical controls, and troubleshoot identity integrations and access-related incidents.

  • Can work effectively with system owners, architects, operations teams, auditors and vendors, and communicate technical risks and recommendations clearly to different audiences.

  • Are organised, outcome-focused and able to maintain clear technical documentation, operating procedures and implementation records.

Good to have

  • Experience with identity governance, privileged access and secrets-management platforms.

  • Experience with cloud IAM, CIEM, identity threat detection and response, non-human identity governance, workload identities or hybrid identity environments.

  • Experience conducting security architecture reviews, threat modelling or risk assessments for Generative AI, agentic AI or other emerging technologies.

  • Proficiency in PowerShell, Python or similar languages for security automation, API integration and orchestration; exposure to infrastructure as code or DevSecOps practices is an advantage.

  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CCSP or equivalent.

Working with stakeholders across the organisation, you will provide cybersecurity advice, conduct security assessments and assurance activities, and support the continuous improvement of the Board’s cybersecurity posture and resilience.

• Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments and security assurance activities across systems, applications, infrastructure, cloud environments and technology initiatives to identify security risks, vulnerabilities and control gaps, assess the adequacy and effectiveness of cybersecurity controls and recommend appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.
• Provide cybersecurity risk and assurance advice to system owners, project teams and other stakeholders, translating findings into practical recommendations and supporting the implementation of appropriate security controls and mitigation measures.

• Analyse and validate penetration testing findings, assess their exploitability and cybersecurity risk, perform or coordinate retesting and validation to ensure identified security vulnerabilities are adequately addressed.
• Leverage penetration testing results together with vulnerability assessments, threat intelligence, External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Adversarial Exposure Validation (AEV) and other technical security assessments to identify systemic security weaknesses and strengthen cybersecurity assurance.
• Explore the use of scripting, automation and data analytics, including Python where appropriate, to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of cybersecurity risk assessment, assurance, monitoring and reporting activities.
• Support and participate in internal and external cybersecurity audits, reviews and regulatory assessments, including the coordination, assessment and remediation of findings.
• Assess compliance with applicable cybersecurity policies, standards, regulatory requirements and industry frameworks, and recommend improvements where necessary.
• Develop, review and enhance cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures and governance frameworks to address evolving cybersecurity risks, regulatory requirements, emerging technologies and organisational needs.

• Experience in conducting cybersecurity risk assessments, security reviews, control assessments and/or other security assurance activities, and recommending appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.

The OSC is a new government agency set up to support the office of the Commissioner of Online Safety (“Commissioner”) established under the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025 (“OSRAA”).

The OSC comprises four teams, namely Case Resolution (“CR”), Investigations (“INV”), Operations Policy (“OP”), and Specialised matters, Appeals and Reconsideration (“SAR”), with CR and INV being the OSC’s two frontline operational units, focused on assisting victims who report online harms get these removed from the internet as well as ensuring compliance with the directions issued by the Commissioner.

Reporting to the Commissioner, the Deputy Commissioner (Operations) is the senior leader responsible for the end-to-end delivery of OSC’s victim complaints operations. This appointment will directly oversee CR and INV, ensuring that OSC’s processes are fair, robust, trauma-informed, evidence-driven and consistent with the OSRAA, while building a high-performing organisation capable of responding to fast-evolving online harms.

You will translate strategic intent into operational reality: designing and refining complaint handling frameworks, overseeing and developing strategies for investigations and case outcomes, setting service standards, and building strong inter-agency and industry operating relationships to achieve effective victim relief.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic leadership and organisational set-up

  • Co-develop OSC’s multi-year operational strategy and implementation roadmap with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team, including the OSC’s operating model, resourcing plan and performance measures.
  • Establish the OSC as a trusted authority for online safety victim complaints through transparent standards, consistent decision-making and measurable service quality.
  • Establish the OSC’s as a global thought leader for online harm victim relief.

Oversee the OSC’s case resolution and investigations (core accountability)

  • Lead and partner with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in owning the end-to-end lifecycle for the reporting of online harms, including intake, triage, evidence gathering, investigations, case assessment, outcomes issuance and post-outcome follow-up.
  • Set and enforce casework quality standards (e.g., timeliness, consistency, proportionality, victim-centred practice, record-keeping and audit trails).
  • Develop investigation protocols and escalation pathways for complex, high-risk or high-impact cases (e.g., coordinated or crossfire harassment, high virality online harmful activity, involving highly vulnerable victims).
  • Drive continuous improvement using case data and trend analysis to refine triage logic, prioritisation rules and operational playbooks.

Operational policy, frameworks and controls

  • Architect and maintain OSC’s operational frameworks and internal policies to implement OSRAA effectively (including guidance, decision frameworks, standard operating procedures and training standards).
  • Ensure strong governance, risk management and internal controls across case operations (including information handling, evidentiary integrity, oversight checks and process assurance).

Stakeholder engagement and ecosystem collaboration

  • Build and sustain effective working relationships with relevant government agencies, technology platforms, app stores, industry partners and community organisations to enable timely victim relief and reduce friction in cross-entity case handling.
  • Represent OSC in operational coordination fora, driving shared protocols and clear lines of accountability during incidents and surges.

People leadership, capability building and culture

  • Build, lead and develop multidisciplinary teams (e.g., case resolution officers, investigators, operations policy officers).
  • Establish a culture of professional rigour, empathy, learning and resilience, including strong supervision practices and quality coaching for case resolution officers.
  • Put in place workforce wellbeing measures, including structured debriefs, vicarious trauma support and safe operating norms for exposure to harmful content.

Corporate leadership and organisational management

  • Provide senior oversight of operational planning and resource allocation; partner corporate functions on workforce planning, budgeting, procurement, performance management and internal communications.
  • Support external communications on OSC’s operations (where appropriate), balancing public assurance with confidentiality and operational sensitivity.
jobRequirements:
Experience and domain expertise

  • At least 10 years’ supervisory experience leading operations, investigations, trust & safety, technology policy, regulatory operations, enforcement, or complex service delivery in public or private sectors.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and running high-volume, high-stakes casework operations with clear service standards and quality controls.
  • Familiarity with how online platforms operate (including content moderation and enforcement processes, reporting tools, recommender systems at a conceptual level, and app ecosystem dynamics). Experience with online trust & safety, public policy, or online content regulation is advantageous.

Leadership and professional competencies

  • Strong judgment and ability to lead decision-making in ambiguous, sensitive and time-critical situations.
  • Excellent stakeholder management—able to build constructive partnerships while holding firm to statutory intent, public interest outcomes and operational integrity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft operational policies, decision rationales, and executive-level briefings.
  • Proven people leader who can build capability, create psychological safety, and enforce high standards of professional conduct and confidentiality.

Resilience and wellbeing

  • You may be exposed to graphic content including (but not limited to) sexual material, minor safety, suicide and self-harm, violent extremism and bullying. Resilience, sound personal coping strategies and commitment to self-care are essential. OSC will support staff through structured wellbeing practices and supervisory safeguards.

Reporting line and working relationship

  • Works closely with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team to ensure coherent end-to-end delivery under OSRAA.
  • Supervises and works with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in overseeing the work of CR and INV.

  • A well-functioning complaints and investigations operation with clear triage, service standards and quality assurance.
  • Consistent, defensible case outcomes with strong victim experience and credible stakeholder confidence.
  • A capable team with established playbooks, training pathways, and wellbeing safeguards.
  • Effective operational relationships across government and industry that improve speed and quality of victim relief.

Position will be commensurate with experience.

jobDescription:
Are you ready to build next-generation, sustainable cold chain logistics for life-saving biopharmaceuticals?

Republic Polytechnic's School of Engineering (SEG), in strategic partnership with industry leader SSW Group, is seeking an ambitious full-time Research Staff (12-month contract) to engineer an industrial-scale 1"m" ^3 self-sustained passive cold storage platform under a DGF-funded initiative.

Current biopharmaceutical distribution relies on massive active energy inputs and heavy daily coolant consumption. This project completely disrupts that model by building a zero-power-in-transit, high-performance thermal container (1"m"×1"m"×1"m" ) capable of locking in sub-zero temperatures (2–8°C) for over 72 continuous hours in harsh tropical environments.

Beyond standard transport, this passive design provides critical fail-safe protection against warehouse power outages and opens up new pathways for long-haul air and sea freight to distant international markets without relying on active electrical refrigeration networks.

You will lead the hands-on engineering across two breakthrough technological pillars:
- Active-Passive "Flash-Charging" Cryogenic System: A rapid-charging base station interface utilizing specialized heat exchangers and Liquid Nitrogen (LN_2) bursts to charge high-density Phase Change Material (PCM) cores and Vacuum Insulated Panels (VIP).
- Triple-Vector IoT Telemetry Engine: An ultra-low-power, cloud-connected sensor matrix tracking real-time Temperature, Relative Humidity, and Oxygen (O_2) levels to ensure absolute data transparency and regulatory compliance (HSA/FDA standards).

The successful candidate will contribute to prototype development, laboratory research, system integration, cold box temperature analysis, field validation at mimic cold storage environment, and technology commercialisation.
jobResponsibilities:
- Perform 3D CAD modelling, understand basic fluid dynamics, and heat exchanger design to eliminate thermal dead zones and maximize LN_2 thermodynamic efficiency across a 1"m" ^3 volume.
- Design, route, and balance high-pressure LN_2 cryogenic pipelines, vacuum-jacketed tubings, manifolds, and automated valve safety systems.
- Build IOT, test, and integrate low-power microcontrollers and sensor arrays (Temp,RH,O_2) with live, cloud-based telemetry dashboards.
- Perform laboratory experiments, cold storage environment trials, temperature and humidity monitoring, passive cold storage box testing, and data analysis.
- Develop, integrate, and evaluate prototype systems, sensors, and instrumentation.
- Collaborate with industry partners to support technology validation and deployment.
- Supervise final-year project students and interns involved in the project.
- Support intellectual property (IP) development, technology transfer, and commercialisation activities.
- Prepare technical reports, journal publications, presentations, and research grant proposals.
- Manage laboratory equipment & consumables, procurement, safety compliance, and research products.
jobRequirements:
- Qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal/Fluid Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Systems Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline.
- Have basic foundational understanding of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer, or cold-chain storage technologies.
- Proficiency in 3D CAD modelling (Autodesk Fusion 360 or SolidWorks) and Design for Manufacturing (DFM) principles.
- Practical skills in embedded electronics, microcontroller programming (Arduino / ESP32), and IoT sensor integration.
- Experience or have interest in cryogenic fluids (LN_2), heat exchangers, or fluid pipeline design is a major advantage.
- A hands-on, proactive mindset with the drive to build physical prototypes and lead projects independently in a dynamic lab environment.
- Strong technical writing and data presentation skills.

jobDescription:
The Division:
Singapore keeps healthcare affordable through government subsidies and the 3Ms: MediShield Life, MediSave and MediFund. For these schemes to work, every part of the supporting systems must function accurately and reliably. 
The Finance Systems Policy (FSP) division at MOH owns the systems that make this possible. These include the National Platform for Healthcare Claims (NPHC), means-testing systems administering healthcare subsidies such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), and the accreditation framework that governs which institutions and practitioners may participate in financing schemes. Together, these systems process tens of thousands of healthcare finance transactions daily and form the operational backbone of Singapore's healthcare financing architecture.

The Role:
You will begin in NPHC, where MediSave and MediShield Life policies are translated into system rules and operational outcomes. The platform processes over 10 million claims annually from public and private hospitals, clinics and other institutions, and interfaces with the Central Provident Fund Board (CPFB), the National Billing System (NBS) used by the public healthcare clusters, Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers, and other MOH systems. Every MediSave deduction and MediShield Life payout and financing computation depends on the system applying the right rules to the right patient at the right time. A rule implemented wrongly means a patient pays the wrong amount and creates downstream reconciliation work for institutions and insurers. Getting the rule right, on the date MOH has committed to publicly, is what this role exists to do.
Over time, as you develop your understanding of FSP's portfolio, there are opportunities to take on other healthcare financing systems. While each system is different, the core responsibilities remain the same: translating policy intent into system behaviour and operational outcomes and ensuring that implementation delivers the intended outcomes for patients, payers and providers. 

You will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time
jobResponsibilities:
Policy Topic Ownership
You will manage a portfolio of healthcare financing policy topics from early policy development through implementation and post-deployment validation. The work starts while the policy is still being formed, not after it is decided. You will work alongside MOH's Healthcare Finance policy divisions to shape policy proposals that can be implemented effectively, then carry the topic through implementation to the point where claims are processed correctly in production. This includes translating policy requirements into system design with vendors and technical teams, refining user stories, testing end-to-end, and confirming the change works before it reaches patients. You will be expected to work independently, surface implementation and operational risks early, and remain accountable for driving each topic through to resolution.

Policy-to-System Translation
Healthcare financing schemes evolve continuously. Claim limits change. New drugs and services become claimable. Deductible, co-insurance and pro-ration parameters are revised. Each change requires someone who understands both the policy intent and constraints and the system behaviour well enough to ensure nothing is lost in translation, and to identify early where a policy cannot be implemented as drafted. A significant part of the role is identifying downstream implementation risks before policy commitments are made. You will be expected to challenge assumptions, surface operational implications, and explain clearly where policy intent and system reality diverge.
You will test business rules against real claims and billing practices, prepare implementation notes that tell institutions, insurers and system partners what is changing and when, and hold that position through consultation. This work is a core responsibility of the role, not a subset of project delivery.

Cross-Party Solutioning
Healthcare financing operates across multiple parties with competing objectives. Policy owners may prioritise policy outcomes. Institutions weigh operational workload and cashflow implications. Insurers focus on claims accuracy and recovery. Technical teams must ensure solutions can be implemented appropriately and sustainably. You will run these consultations directly across public and private institutions, the IP insurers, NBS and its vendors, and CPFB. Your role is not to satisfy every stakeholder. Your role is to structure competing considerations, lead discussions towards workable solutions, and recommend a clear implementation position that balances policy intent, operational feasibility and system integrity, including when that position is not the option stakeholders initially preferred. 

Operational Continuity and Analytics
Implementation does not end at deployment. You will monitor deployed changes after production rollout, investigate production issues, and analyse claims and system data yourself to validate implementation outcomes: how utilisation changed, whether payouts moved as expected, and whether unintended consequences emerged. You will be expected to trace issues to their root causes, validate outcomes using evidence, and use data to inform future policy and system decisions.
This is not a project coordination role. Success is measured by the quality of your judgment, the soundness of your recommendations, and whether the implemented system behaviour reflects the intended policy outcome. The role requires genuine ownership of both the policy intent behind a change and the system logic that carries it out.

The Team:
You will report to an Assistant Director within FSP and work alongside a division of about 14 officers. You are expected to work across NPHC workstreams covering policy development and implementation, as well as the introduction of new system features and capabilities.

FSP runs a structured capability development programme for its officers, built around four areas: product thinking, policy domain knowledge, communications, and technical skills. In practical terms, within 9 months, you should be able to: read a policy proposal and identify implementation risks before development begins, hold your own in a technical design review with vendors and system teams, lead discussions across policy teams, institutions and insurers, analyse claims outcomes and explain what happened, why it happened and whether the result is consistent with policy intent, and produce recommendations that help Senior Management make sound decisions.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone with 3 to 5 years of working experience in policy, operations, technology, analytics or a field that requires structured problem solving across multiple domains.

Beyond that, what matters is how you think. You should be able to develop a clear position from incomplete information, test it against evidence, and communicate it clearly, and adjust it when new facts emerge. 

Key competencies required:
•	Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements. In FSP, this means tracing financing outcomes from policy intent through business rules, system logic and claims behaviour, and determining whether the outcomes are correct. You will be expected to develop evidence-based recommendations and advise Senior Management and stakeholders on policy implementation options and trade-offs. You should be comfortable with numbers, as much of the role involves validating the results of financing computations using real operational data.
•	Learning and Putting Skills into Action. Healthcare financing is a domain you build over time. What matters is your willingness to understand it rigorously and to apply what you learn and continue building expertise in an environment where the impact on patients and healthcare providers is real.
•	Improving and Innovating. FSP's systems serve a policy landscape that changes continuously. You should be able to identify where a process or system has not kept pace and propose practical improvements while managing implementation risks.
•	Working Effectively with Stakeholders. NPHC operates across MOH, CPFB, the public healthcare clusters, private medical institutions, insurers and system partners. You should be able to work across these stakeholders to achieve clear, workable and sustainable outcomes.
•	Communicating Clearly: You should have strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex policy and system issues and recommendations clearly

Your background is less important than how you approach problems. That said, the following thinking patterns tend to predict success in this role:
•	You enjoy working across policy development, operations and technical implementation.
•	You are curious about how large systems work and naturally want to understand why something happened rather than accepting that it happened. 
•	You are comfortable working through ambiguity and incomplete information.
•	You prefer owning a problem end-to-end rather than handing it off once a recommendation is made.
•	You build your views from evidence rather than consensus.
•	You see stakeholder complexity as a problem to be structured and solved.
Prior experience in healthcare, the public sector, or a regulated industry is useful but not required. Familiarity with Singapore's healthcare financing schemes (MediSave, MediShield Life, CHAS) is a genuine advantage.

What we can offer you
This role provides exposure to policy development, large-scale system implementation, data-driven decision making and stakeholder engagement within a single posting. You will work with policy divisions, healthcare institutions, insurers and technology vendors while developing the ability to operate across policy, operations and technology domains.

jobResponsibilities:
The SOC Product Lead is the strategic owner of the Cybersecurity Operations Centre's detection and monitoring capabilities, treating the SOC as a continuously evolving product rather than a static operational function. This role bridges business risk, stakeholder demands, compliance obligations, and the threat landscape — translating them into a prioritised roadmap that the Tech Lead and analyst teams execute against. The Product Lead does not build detection rules; they ensure the right capabilities are built, in the right order, for the right outcomes.​

SOC Capability Roadmap & Backlog Ownership

  • Define, own, and continuously refine the SOC capability roadmap — encompassing detection use cases, automation workflows, tooling enhancements, and analyst enablement initiatives
  • Maintain a prioritised product backlog that balances immediate operational risk reduction with longer-term platform maturity goals
  • Write clear user stories and acceptance criteria for detection use cases, SOAR playbooks, and dashboard requirements — in a format the Tech Lead and engineering team can act on
  • Facilitate sprint planning, backlog refinement, and sprint review ceremonies in collaboration with the Tech Lead and Design Lead
  • Track and report delivery velocity, sprint outcomes, and roadmap progress to SOC management and security leadership​

Stakeholder Management & Requirements Gathering

  • Act as the primary interface between the SOC and internal stakeholders
  • Conduct regular stakeholder engagement sessions to surface new monitoring requirements, regulatory obligations, and threat concerns
  • Translate ambiguous business risk statements into concrete, actionable SOC capability requirements
  • Manage stakeholder expectations on delivery timelines, scope trade-offs, and prioritisation decisions
  • Represent the SOC's capability roadmap in governance forums, risk committees, and security steering group meetings​

Threat-Informed Prioritisation

  • Maintain a continuous threat landscape assessment — incorporating inputs from threat intelligence feeds, red team findings, incident post-mortems, industry ISACs, and regulatory advisories
  • Prioritise detection use case development based on threat actor relevance, asset criticality, and exploitability — mapped to the MITRE ATT&CK framework
  • Own the detection coverage gap register, working with the Tech Lead to close high-priority gaps within agreed sprint cycles
  • Ensure new and emerging threat vectors (e.g., AI-assisted attacks, supply chain compromise, cloud-native threats) are reflected in the backlog ahead of operational need​

Tool & Vendor Strategy

  • Own the SOC technology budget — forecasting spend, managing renewals, and justifying investment cases to leadership​

Metrics, Reporting & Continuous Improvement

  • Define and own the SOC's key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics — including MTTD, MTTR, alert fidelity, use case coverage, and automation rates
  • Develop and maintain executive-facing dashboards and reports that communicate SOC effectiveness in business risk terms, not purely technical metrics
  • Lead regular operational reviews — identifying trends, persistent gaps, and improvement opportunities across people, process, and technology dimensions
  • Conduct use case lifecycle reviews to retire outdated rules, refresh low-fidelity detections, and ensure the detection library remains current and relevant
  • Drive post-incident reviews from a product improvement perspective — ensuring lessons learned are converted into backlog items and delivered

Compliance & Governance Alignment

  • Ensure SOC monitoring coverage aligns with applicable regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements (e.g., MAS TRM, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, local IM8 guidelines where applicable)
  • Maintain traceability between compliance control requirements and deployed detection use cases

The Deputy Director, Enterprise Data Services leads ACRA’s enterprise data services function and supports the System Owner for ACRA’s entity data platform serving Whole-of-Government (WOG).

• Ensure the platform and data services are reliable, scalable, secure and sustainable.

• Lead the delivery and administration of WOG data-sharing services, including APIs and other data access mechanisms.
• Oversee the assessment, prioritisation and delivery of WOG data requests and required data transformations.
• Review agency data requests through relevant data-sharing frameworks and coordinate required Data Owner and CDO approvals.

• Drive Master Data Management (MDM) and establish data quality metrics, controls and improvement measures.
• Oversee governance of data definitions, lineage, transformation logic and data-sharing arrangements.
• Work with Data Owners to establish clear accountability for data quality and appropriate use.
• Ensure compliance with applicable data governance, security and regulatory requirements.

4. Stakeholder & Regulatory Engagement
• Lead engagement with government agencies, Data Owners and other stakeholders on data-sharing requirements and priorities.
• Assess the impact of new regulatory regimes and policies involving new or changed data submissions to ACRA and translate these into platform and data-service requirements.
• Coordinate with Data Owners, Data Consumer Agencies (DCAs) and vendors on data-sharing boundaries, specifications and implementation.

5. Service & Vendor Management
• Oversee the ongoing operation of the platform and data services, ensuring service quality, reliability and continuity.
• Drive continuous improvement based on service performance, data quality, operational issues and user needs.
• Oversee vendors and delivery partners against agreed service levels and outcomes.
• Ensure appropriate assurance activities, including periodic security, governance and code reviews.

6. Team Leadership
• Lead and develop the Enterprise Data Services team, setting priorities and building capabilities in enterprise data management and data services.
• Provide leadership and guidance on enterprise data-sharing matters across ACRA.
• Support departmental planning, resource prioritisation and capability development.
jobRequirements:
• Professional qualifications in Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Management, Engineering or a related discipline.

jobDescription:
The Finance and Facilities Division (FFD) is responsible for the Ministry’s financial matters, procurement management and facilities development and management. FFD promotes prudent stewardship of the Ministry’s resources by applying sound governance controls and best practices across its various functions. 

The Finance Branch provides financial stewardship and partnership by optimising resource allocation and management, while ensuring sound financial administration. The Budget Team plays a key role in driving MSF's resource strategy, financial sustainability and medium-term planning.
jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for an analytical team player to partner with the Assistant Director (Budget Team) in shaping and managing the Ministry’s budget and resource strategy. In this role, you will work closely with internal stakeholders and the Ministry of Finance (MOF), lead budget planning and submissions, analyse financial information, and provide strategic advice to guide resource decisions.

You will also identify and drive process improvements, including the use of data, technology, and AI-enabled tools, to strengthen budget management and improve service delivery.

The scope of budget and resource management will primarily cover MSF’s annual and medium-term budget planning, resource allocation, expenditure management, financial analysis and reporting, as well as the development of data-driven insights to support strategic decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:
You will partner with the Assistant Director and work with stakeholders to:

•	Coordinate annual and medium-term budget planning, resource allocation, and budget submissions. 
•	Monitor budget utilisation and expenditure trends and highlight emerging issues for timely follow-up. 
•	Analyse financial information and prepare clear recommendations to support management decisions.
•	 Work with internal stakeholders and MOF to address funding matters, clarify requirements, and support the timely resolution of resource issues.
•	Drive process improvement and innovation in budget management, including the use of data, technology, and AI-enabled tools. 
•	Support projects and initiatives to strengthen budgeting capabilities, reporting, and service delivery.
jobRequirements:
•	Tertiary qualification, preferably with relevant experience in budgeting, financial planning, or public sector finance.
•	Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate financial information into practical recommendations.
•	Ability to work effectively with stakeholders and communicate clearly in writing and discussions.
•	Interest and experience in process improvement, digitalisation, data analytics, or the use of technology and AI tools.
•	Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and contribute effectively as part of a team.
•	Self-motivated and able to thrive in a dynamic environment.

Functional Competencies:
•	Resource and Budget Planning
•	Financial Analysis and Reporting
•	Financial Governance, Controls and Expenditure Management 
•	Stakeholder Partnership and MOF Engagement
•	Data Analytics, AI Enablement and Process Improvement

jobDescription:
As a Senior/ Intelligence Officer/ Assistant Intelligence Officer, Field Intelligence at the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), you will be part of a team conducting intelligence operations into breaches and potential breaches of HSA legislation and regulatory standards.

You will work on the ground to gather, develop and assess intelligence and provide timely and actionable intelligence to support enforcement operations and decision-making. The role involves field intelligence gathering, ground engagement, observation, and operational support, with deployment across different environments depending on operational requirements.
jobResponsibilities:
• Gather, develop and assess ground intelligence on potential breaches of HSA legislation and regulatory standards, including identifying persons, entities and activities of interest.
  • Proactively maintain a pulse on the ground to identify and assess emerging issues, incidents and trends that may warrant further attention or enforcement action.
  • Analyse information from various sources to identify patterns, risks and connections, and translate findings into actionable leads, assessments and recommendations.
  • Prepare timely and accurate intelligence reports, assessments and briefings for management and operational teams.
  • Support the planning and conduct of intelligence-led operations, including joint operations with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with relevant government agencies and partners to support intelligence sharing and operational coordination.
  • Handle sensitive information with discretion and ensure all activities are conducted in accordance with established policies, procedures and applicable legal requirements.
  • Perform other intelligence and operational duties as required to support HSA's enforcement objectives.
jobRequirements:
• At least 5 years of relevant experience in enforcement, regulatory, intelligence, investigation or related operational functions.
  • Strong interpersonal and networking skills, with the ability to engage effectively and build rapport with people from diverse backgrounds.
  • Keen observation skills and situational awareness, with the ability to recognise and assess information of potential intelligence value.
  • Analytical and inquisitive, with the ability to identify connections and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Resourceful, adaptable and able to work independently as well as effectively within an operational team.
  • Sound judgement, discretion and integrity in handling sensitive information and operational matters.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear and concise intelligence reports.
  • Comfortable with field-based work and prepared to work beyond normal office hours or on weekends when operationally required.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
  • A valid Class 2B and/or Class 3 driving licence will be an advantage.
  • Ability to converse in additional languages or dialects will be an added advantage.

Please only apply if you are able to meet the operational requirements.

The successful candidate will be offered a 1-year contract (with option for automatic renewal for a further one year) in the first instance.

Shortlisted candidates would be contacted within 30 days from the closing date of the advertisement. We regret that only shortlisted candidates would be notified.

jobDescription:
Digital forensics plays an important role in generating leads for investigators to track down criminals and uncover digital evidence to support the prosecution of these criminals.

The officer will be part of the Digital Forensics team in the Technology Investigation Support Division (TISD) that performs digital forensics investigations such as data acquisition, evidence recovery and forensics examination of digital devices in support of investigation and prosecution. Additional responsibilities may also include assisting in managing the forensics laboratory and its supporting infrastructure as well as to identify new technologies to enhance forensics analysis.
jobResponsibilities:
Perform Digital Forensics examination and analysis into a wide range of devices in support of investigation and prosecution.

  • Conduct thorough digital forensics seizures, preservation and examination of digital evidence from devices, operating systems and/or networks and ensure all forensic processes comply with legal, procedural, and evidentiary standards.
  • Properly identify, collect, label, document, store, and manage digital evidence in accordance with established procedures. Maintain complete chain-of-custody records.
  • Document detailed findings. Provide objective assessment of digital evidence and to recommend appropriate opinion on assessment of evidence to stakeholders.
  • Create comprehensive, court-ready forensic reports and provide expert testimony in court to support investigative teams in evidence presentation.
  • Work closely with investigating officers, legal officers to scope forensic requirements and assist in identifying investigative leads based on digital evidence.

Ensure proper use and maintenance of forensic tools. Ensuring up-to-date SOPs and consistent processes.

  • Manage and maintain forensic laboratory tools, systems, licenses, and inventories.
  • Develop, review and maintain SOPs and investigative processes; recommend and implement process improvements. Support digital evidence handling policies, chain-of-custody protocols and accreditation requirements.

Ensure continuous capability training and development. Keep abreast of emerging technology and threat awareness

  • Keep skills current through training, certification and professional development. Identify training needs and support knowledge transfer within the unit.
  • Contribute to knowledge-sharing, mentoring and training of staff and stakeholders, where appropriate.
  • Monitor developments and identify new trends, stay up-to-date with evolving digital technologies, emerging threats, forensic methods, and legal precedents.
  • Assess implications of new technologies on forensic readiness and investigation approaches.

Establish operational collaboration with other Law Enforcement Agencies, (e.g. Interpol, SPF, HSA, IRAS, CPIB, MOM, CNB, Singapore Customs, and other agencies in DFG).

  • Establish and maintain a network of liaison contacts with other law enforcement agencies to exchange information, best practices, experience and expertise, etc.
  • Collaborate and co-ordinate with other agencies in joint enforcement and investigations, etc.
jobRequirements:
• A background referably in Digital Forensics, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Computer Science or any other relevant discipline.
  • Minimum of 2–5 years of professional experience in digital forensics, incident response, or cybersecurity.
  • Proficiency with industry-standard forensic tools such as Cellebrite, Magnet AXIOM, Autopsy/Sleuth Kit, Oxygen Forensic Detective, EnCase, FTK, MSAB XRY etc.
  • Ability to acquire and analyze data from Computers (Windows, macOS, Linux), mobile devices (iOS, Android), cloud environments, network storage, memory dumps, volatile data and IoT devices.
  • Possession of a good understanding of forensic artefacts in operating systems, file systems, data recover technology and forensic investigation procedures.
  • Proficient in scripting and automation (e.g., Python, PowerShell, Bash) to enhance forensic workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience in lab management, forensic acquisition, analysis, and reporting of digital evidence.
  • Possession of professional certifications or industry-recognised qualification related to Digital Forensics such as Cellebrite Certified Physical Analyst (CCPA), Magnet Certified Forensic Examiner (MCFE), EnCase Certified Examiner (EnCE), GIAC Advance Smartphone Forensics (GASF), GIAC Certified Battlefield Forensics and Acquisition (GBFA), GIAC Certified Forensic Examiner (GCFE) or GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA) would be advantageous.
  • Strong analytical skills, meticulous, resourceful, independent and objective, and with an inquisitive mind.
  • Effective team player, with good inter-personal and communication skills.
  • Self-motivated, driven and willingness to take up new challenges or additional responsibilities with keen interest in ongoing learning and professional development.
  • Adaptability and ability to work under pressure and tight deadlines.
  • High standards of professionalism and personal integrity.
  • May require to work at extended hours or be on-call as necessary to meet operational needs.

Please only apply if you are able to meet the operational requirements.

jobDescription:
You will be part of a team responsible for strengthening crime scene management and forensic response capabilities in support of investigation, enforcement and intelligence operations.

As a Crime Scene Forensic officer, you will support the proper management, documentation, examination and processing of crime scenes, ensuring that potential evidence is identified, preserved, recovered and handled in a manner that maintains evidential integrity and supports downstream forensic examination and court proceedings.

You will work closely with investigators, forensic specialists, enforcement officers and other stakeholders to provide operational support at scenes, develop crime scene processes, and uplift forensic awareness and competency across frontline and investigative units.
jobResponsibilities:
Crime Scene Response and Management

  • Attend and support the management of crime scenes, incident scenes and other scenes of forensic interest.
  • Conduct systematic assessment, documentation, photography, sketching, search, recovery and preservation of physical and trace evidence.
  • Ensure proper scene control, contamination prevention, safety management and preservation of evidential value.
  • Advise officers on proper handling, packaging, labelling and submission of exhibits.
  • Maintain chain of custody, documentation and accountability for all recovered exhibits.

Forensic Support to Investigations

  • Work with investigators and forensic specialists to identify evidence sources and appropriate forensic strategies.
  • Support collection and preservation of evidence including biological traces, fingerprints, footwear marks, tool marks, fibres, documents, weapons and electronic devices.
  • Prepare scene documentation, reports, statements and materials for investigation or court purposes.
  • Provide operational input to case reviews, event reconstruction and investigative decision-making.

Capability Development and Process Improvement

  • Develop and review crime scene management workflows, SOPs, checklists, equipment lists and evidence-handling procedures.
  • Validate, evaluate and implement new crime scene equipment, techniques and technologies.
  • Participate in exercises, trials and after-action reviews.
  • Identify operational gaps and propose improvements to crime scene response, evidence recovery and forensic coordination.

Training and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Plan and deliver forensic awareness and crime scene management training for officers. Develop training materials, practical scenarios and competency-based assessments.
  • Engage internal and external stakeholders to promote good crime scene practices and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Document lessons learnt, good practices and operational learning points.

Governance, Quality and Readiness

  • Ensure crime scene processes comply with established procedures, safety requirements, legal considerations and evidential standards.
  • Maintain readiness of crime scene equipment, consumables, response kits and operational resources.
  • Support audits, reviews and quality assurance activities.
  • Keep abreast of developments in forensic science and crime scene investigation methods.
jobRequirements:
• A background in forensic science, life sciences, chemistry, biology, criminology, criminal justice, security studies or a related discipline is preferred.
  • Certification or training in crime scene investigation, forensic science, workplace safety, photography or evidence management would be advantageous.
  • Experience in crime scene work, forensic examination, investigation, enforcement operations, laboratory operations or evidence management is advantageous.
  • Prior experience in crime scene processing, forensic photography, evidence recovery, fingerprint development, trace evidence handling or exhibit management is a strong advantage.
  • Familiarity with forensic laboratory processes, investigation workflows, chain of custody requirements and court processes is desirable.
  • High level of integrity, professionalism and discretion in handling sensitive information and exhibits.
  • Meticulous approach to evidence handling, record keeping and procedural compliance.
  • Strong observational, analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-disciplinary team.
  • Good situational awareness and ability to operate under time-sensitive or operationally challenging conditions.
  • Physically fit and prepared to attend scenes and support operational deployments.
  • Willingness to work irregular hours and respond to scenes when required.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and capability development.

jobDescription:
Social media today is no longer a supporting channel — it is where culture is made, influence is built, and travel decisions are shaped. For STB, this shift represents a significant opportunity to lead in destination marketing through sharp, insight-driven social strategy that is both creative and commercially grounded.

As the Social Strategist, you will be the resident expert on social strategy within STB's social department — developing the frameworks, playbooks, and strategic direction that the wider team builds upon. This is a role for someone who thinks deeply about where social is heading, translates that thinking into clear and actionable strategy, and is equally comfortable getting hands-on to deliver. You will work across the department and with key external partners to ensure STB's social presence is coherent, forward-looking, and effective.
jobResponsibilities:
Social Strategy Development & Oversight

You will develop, review, and own the overarching social strategy that guides the department's work. This means producing the strategic frameworks and playbooks that team members plug into as they develop strategies for their respective workstreams — ensuring that individual efforts are aligned, coherent, and laddering up to a unified social vision. You will regularly review and evolve the strategy in response to performance data, platform shifts, and broader marketing objectives, serving as the strategic backbone and thought partner for the team.

Performance Measurement & Reporting

You will own the performance for the Visit Singapore (VS) social channels. Working with the in-house social media manager, you will ensure monthly performance reports on VS channels are produced consistently and on time, and that the data is translated into clear insights and recommendations. Beyond the monthly cadence, you will lead quarterly and annual reviews — analysing performance trends, identifying what is working and what needs to change, and presenting findings to relevant stakeholders.

Channel Mix & Platform Planning

A core part of your remit is ensuring STB is investing in the right platforms at the right time. You will conduct yearly reviews of the social channel mix, assessing each platform's performance, audience fit, and strategic relevance — tracking cultural, platform, and algorithm shifts and translating them into a formal set of recommendations that shape how the department allocates its resources going forward.

Emerging Platforms, Experimentation & Prospecting

You will proactively scan for emerging channels, closed communities, and new social spaces that present strategic opportunities for STB. Critically, you will not just identify these opportunities — you will lead and run the pilots, developing go-to-market approaches, executing the test, and producing a clear assessment of viability and scalability. Where a pilot proves successful, you may continue to own and manage that channel as part of your portfolio. This requires a structured yet experimental mindset — knowing how to design a meaningful test, read the results honestly, and make a clear recommendation. You will also take the lead on horizon-scanning for the social department, synthesising signals from across the industry into actionable foresight that informs both near-term strategy and longer-term planning.

Campaign Delivery

You will be involved in developing key campaigns, driving the delivery of social strategy from planning through to execution. This means working across functions to ensure that the strategic intent of a campaign is preserved through to delivery and being hands-on where needed to make it happen.

Paid Social Oversight

Working closely with the Digital and Media team, you will oversee STB's paid social strategy, ensuring that paid efforts are meaningfully integrated with organic activity and aligned to campaign objectives.

jobDescription:

As a result, there exists a need to strengthen the pipeline of skilled cybersecurity professionals through identifying and empowering individuals with cybersecurity aptitude and good learning attitude to take on cybersecurity roles. 

CSA’s Cybersecurity Development Programme (CSDP) is a 12-month programme designed to develop both fresh graduates and working professionals into cybersecurity talents in the public sector, with the aim of building cybersecurity capabilities to secure Singapore’s digital economy and infrastructure.
jobResponsibilities:
CSDP is a 12-month programme that consists of two phases: a 1-month classroom training phase, followed by an 11-month job posting.*

*Please note that the programme curriculum may be subject to change (including programme duration/training curriculum, etc). The programme stated below is accurate as of August 2026.

Phase 1: Classroom Training

CSDP officers will undergo a rigorous curriculum in their first month to build both technical and professional capabilities. Officers will undergo courses that will lead to cybersecurity certifications such as:

•	SANS SEC504
•	SANS ICS310
•	Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate

Officers will also receive training in professional skills such as Stakeholder Management and Effective Writing in the Public Service.

Phase 2: Job Posting

After the classroom training phase, CSDP officers will be posted to a CSA division or partner government agency for the remaining 11 months. During their posting, officers will gain hands-on experience in mainly one of these cybersecurity domains:

•	Malware Analysis
•	Digital Forensics & Incident Response
•	Emerging Technologies
•	Penetration Testing
•	Cybersecurity Solutions and Consultancy
•	Cybersecurity Operations Centre
•	Threat Intelligence
•	Governance, Risk and Compliance

Job postings will take into consideration each candidate’s interests, suitability and cybersecurity manpower needs across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). Further assessments may be required to determine a candidate’s suitability for specific roles, and the final posting decision rests with CSA.

Gain Exposure Beyond Your Posting

Throughout the programme, CSDP officers will have opportunities to work on cybersecurity projects at the national level, undergo further technical and non-technical training, and engage with recognised industry partners and the public.

These experiences will enable officers to broaden their cybersecurity expertise, develop valuable professional networks and contribute towards strengthening Singapore’s cybersecurity posture.

Upon successful completion of the 12-month programme, CSDP officers may continue their employment with CSA or be forward deployed to another government agency, subject to satisfactory performance and successful matching to a suitable role across the Whole-of-Government (WOG).

CSA is currently located at the Punggol Digital District.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for individuals who are passionate about cybersecurity, eager to develop technical expertise, and motivated by the opportunity to contribute to Singapore’s cybersecurity and national cyber defence.

What we look for in this entry-level position:

•	A keen interest and demonstrated aptitude in cybersecurity and technology, with a strong willingness to learn and continuously develop new technical capabilities.

•	A good foundation in computing and cybersecurity concepts, such as computer networks, operating systems, programming, information security or network architecture.

•	An interest in applying technical knowledge to real-world cybersecurity challenges and national-level cybersecurity work.

•	Open and adaptable to working across different cybersecurity domains and job roles, based on individual suitability and the cybersecurity needs of the Whole-of-Government.

•	A strong interest in public service and contributing to Singapore’s cybersecurity mission.

•	Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with the curiosity to investigate unfamiliar problems and develop practical solutions.

•	Able to communicate ideas clearly and explain technical concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

•	Able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team in a dynamic environment.

While not mandatory, candidates who demonstrate their interest and capabilities in cybersecurity through any of the following will have an advantage:

•	Cybersecurity or relevant technical certifications;
•	Capture The Flag (CTF) competitions;
•	Hackathons or technology competitions;
•	Cybersecurity projects, internships or research;
•	Online cybersecurity courses or credentials;
•	Personal technical projects, labs or cybersecurity-related portfolios; or

Above all, we are looking for candidates who demonstrate strong potential, a genuine interest in cybersecurity, a positive learning attitude and a desire to secure Singapore's digital future.

Incident Response Leadership

•	Prepare and maintain accurate incident reports, situation updates and timely communications for internal stakeholders and regulatory authorities, where required.

jobDescription:
Singapore Tourism Board's Data Exploration and Partnerships (DXP) department is shaping the data landscape for Singapore's tourism sector, and this role is central to that mission.

As our Data Partnerships Manager, you will identify tourism industry data needs, forge strategic data partnerships, and design data use cases that generate actionable insights for STB and the broader tourism ecosystem. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of partnerships development, data strategy and analysis, and industry transformation.

Success in this position means building a robust ecosystem of data partnerships that delivers measurable value to Singapore's tourism sector, while progressively elevating the industry's data capability. You will serve as the bridge between STB's strategic data needs and the broader tourism ecosystem, ensuring that partnerships and data exploration initiatives translate into insights that drive real tourism outcomes. You will report directly to the Head of Department and work closely with line units across STB, government agencies, and industry partners.

What makes this role unique is the breadth of impact it offers: brokering strategic data partnerships, designing and running data pilots that surface actionable insights, and guiding tourism businesses in translating data into real business decisions. All of this within a newly established department where you will help shape how we work and make an impact on Singapore's tourism data landscape.
jobResponsibilities:
Board wide Data Needs Assessment and Coordination
You will consolidate and review data needs from line units across Singapore Tourism Board, conducting comprehensive gap analysis and research to fulfill data gaps within STB. This involves facilitating requirements gathering with line units and external stakeholders, researching data providers in the market, prioritising data requirements based on business impact, and coordinating across departments to resolve overlapping data needs and build a consolidated view of STB's data landscape. You will synthesise these findings into a prioritised data acquisition pipeline that guides STB’s data acquisition and partnership decisions.


Data Partnership Development and Management
You will proactively identify, evaluate, and establish strategic data partnerships with tourism industry players, technology providers, and government agencies. This includes building and maintaining a pipeline of prospective partners, conducting market research, assessing the commercial and strategic value of partnership opportunities, leading negotiations, and structuring agreements that deliver mutual benefit and long-term sustainability.

Beyond establishing partnerships, you will manage ongoing partner relationships to ensure continued value creation, and work with internal departments to develop the governance and processes that underpin our Data Partnerships work, including frameworks, standard operating procedures, partnership templates, and performance monitoring mechanisms. All partnership activities need to be conducted in compliance with data protection regulations and government policies, with best practices documented and scaled across multiple arrangements.


Data Use Case Design and Pilot Implementation
You will design new data use cases that demonstrate the business value of tourism data, including working closely with internal and external stakeholders to define hypotheses, dataset requirements, success metrics, resource requirements, and implementation timelines. You will plan and execute end-to-end data pilots, which involve setting up small-scale data pipelines and data ingestion processes, performing data transformation and calculations, exploratory data analysis, creating dashboards, and generating analysis and insights that inform tourism strategy and operations. You will document pilot findings and translate results into clear recommendations on whether and how to scale successful use cases into sustainable data products on STAN, our core data and analytics platform.


Industry Capability Building
You will design and deliver industry engagement programmes that equip tourism businesses with the knowledge and skills to use STB's data assets and insights for practical business decision-making. This includes conducting outreach and training sessions that guide industry stakeholders — such as hotels, attractions, and tour operators — in interpreting and applying tourism data to their specific business contexts, whether to sharpen their marketing strategies, inform product development, or identify new visitor segments.

To ensure these programmes are targeted and effective, you will assess the data capability and maturity levels of Singapore's tourism industry, mapping existing skills, tools, and practices to identify gaps. Based on these findings, you will develop capability uplift plans, training materials, and long-term strategies that progressively build the industry's ability to leverage data for competitive advantage, while also strengthening STB's internal data capabilities.

You will track and measure the impact of these initiatives using data maturity assessments and engagement outcomes, and contribute to positioning STB as a trusted thought leader and enabler in tourism data capability through publications, industry events, and sector-wide initiatives.

This includes vulnerabilities to disruptions to day-to-day life, social divisions, and coercion to act against our national interest. Such risks impact multiple sectors and require multi-sector responses to effectively mitigate risks to Singapore. NSCS also works with agencies to anticipate and identify emergent security risks, and to build up capabilities and resources to deal with these. NSCS supports the Coordinating Minister for National Security, and Permanent Secretary (National Security Intelligence Coordination).

The role will give you the opportunity to strengthen:

o	Critical Thinking: You will need to keep abreast of national security developments and synthesise information across domains (geopolitical, economic, social, environment, information, etc.) to identify and analyse cross-cutting national security risks. These include economic security risks, digital security risks, concentration risks, and inter-dependency risks.
o	Systems Thinking: You will need to integrate analysis of external developments with assessments of Singapore’s vulnerabilities and how the latter will change over time. You will recommend the best way to structure the Whole-of-Government response to the risk. This will require you to suggest constructive solutions which balance multiple policy considerations across domains. For specific risks, you could contribute to the full policy value-chain from strategic planning, policy formulation, policy-operations, to comms and implementation (e.g., legislation).
o	Influence: You will need to mobilise colleagues from a wide range of agencies, with different mandates and policy considerations, to work with you on the overall risk assessment. You will need to build consensus on the risk level Singapore can live with and the Whole-of-Government action needed to mitigate the risks. This would require you to build extensive and deep networks across domains and seniority levels, and develop a deep understanding of their considerations and constraints.

Depending on your performance and experience, you could be given the opportunity to lead a team (of 2-3 officers) or project, and individually handle complex and sensitive policy pieces that cut across NSCS’s work.
jobResponsibilities:
The policy teams in NSCS looks across: 

o	[Policy 1] Geostrategic issues that pose existential risks to Singapore, spanning economic security, technology dependencies, manpower risks, geopolitical sensitivities, space matters, and other related issues.
o	[Policy 2] Critical infrastructure and interdependencies, including risks and vulnerabilities arising from the energy transition, climate change and digital dependencies.
o	[Policy 3] Social cohesion, resilience and public confidence, focusing on cross-cutting issues relating to social cohesion and resilience (SCR) that threaten national security, including foreign interference and influence, with a data-centric approach to drive policy shifts.

You will work in a policy team / lead a policy team:

o	To hunt out Singapore’s cross-cutting vulnerabilities (e.g., in critical infrastructure, social resilience) that could be exploited/ disrupted and build shared risk pictures (through policy analysis and/ or data analysis) to inform decision-making by public sector leaders.
o	To mobilise collective Whole-of-Government efforts to tackle complex, collective-action problems. This could involve putting forth recommendations to achieve better national outcomes through balancing differing policy objectives

agencyDescription:
Yellow Ribbon Singapore
Formerly known as Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE), Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) is a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs. Our purpose is to help inmates and ex-offenders rebuild their lives and lower the recidivism rate through skills and long term career development, with an effective Aftercare support network. As the lead agency championing Hope, Forgiveness, Acceptance and Second Chances for ex-offenders, we strive towards building a safer and more inclusive Singapore.

Beyond Second Chances
Without second chances, a released offender will leave the first physical prison and find himself entering into a second social prison. Therefore, it is not enough to give an offender a skill, we need to offer him a job that can lead to a long-term career. It is not enough to ask an offender to renounce his gang and past, his family needs to accept him back, and the community must be ready to reintegrate him. However, ex-offenders are not mere recipients of second chances. When successfully reintegrated, they can pay it forward and actively give back to the community too. As individuals, or collectively as a community. Individuals, organisations and employers do not just offer second chances when they can accept an ex-offender. In fact, their actions inspire others as well. Together, our collective effort can build a safer and more inclusive society. 

At Yellow Ribbon Singapore, we aim to build a community where ex-offenders are empowered to look beyond their past and towards the future. The journey is for them to make but we ensure that it would not be a lonely one. Join us, as we embark on this exciting journey of Beyond Second Chances. Be part of the YRSG family, together we can support the Yellow Ribbon cause and inspire collective action for a more inclusive and safer Singapore.

jobDescription:
The Competency-Driven Growth Office (CDGO) in the Public Service Division drives the Public Service’s shift towards Competency-Driven Growth (CDG), where officers’ growth and development are anchored on competencies — the skills, knowledge and behaviours needed to perform and grow in their roles. 

 

As Manager / Senior Manager in CDGO, you will anchor how the CDG story comes together and is experienced by officers across the Public Service. CDG comprises different policies, programmes, tools and initiatives that support officers in their growth and development. A key part of this role is to connect these different efforts into a coherent narrative, so that officers understand not just individual initiatives, but how they fit together and what CDG means for their own growth and careers. You will work closely with the PSD Communications team and Clusters within PSD to shape and implement this narrative and find practical and engaging ways to bring CDG to life for officers.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Steward the CDG narrative 

Develop and maintain a clear and coherent narrative for CDG, connecting the various policies, programmes, tools and initiatives that contribute to officers’ growth and development. 

Work across PSD teams to identify the common threads across different initiatives and translate them into a story that makes sense from an officer’s perspective. 

Help teams position individual initiatives within the broader CDG narrative, so that communications reinforce rather than fragment the overall employee experience. 

Translate complex or policy-heavy concepts into simple, relatable messages that help officers understand what CDG means for them and how they can take charge of their career development. 

Maintain coherence in the CDG narrative as policies and programmes evolve. 

2. Bring CDG to life for officers 

Develop and implement the CDG communications approaches that make CDG tangible, relevant and useful to officers. 

Identify the moments, channels and formats through which officers can encounter and understand CDG, moving beyond awareness towards helping officers take meaningful action for their own growth. 

Develop practical resources, content and experiences that show officers how competencies connect to everyday aspects of their careers — such as understanding their strengths and gaps, having regular career conversations, identifying development opportunities and taking actions to grow. 

Surface stories, examples and practices that demonstrate what competency-driven growth looks like in practice. 

Test and refine communications based on how officers understand and respond to them. 
 

3. Connect communications across CDG initiatives 

Maintain an overview of major CDG-related initiatives and communications across relevant PSD teams. 

Identify opportunities to sequence, connect or consolidate communications so that officers experience CDG as a coherent journey rather than a series of separate programmes. 

Work with initiative owners to sharpen the officer-facing proposition of their work and ensure alignment with the broader CDG narrative. 

Support key CDGO communications and milestones, including presentations, campaigns, resource packs and other officer-facing materials. 

4. Strengthen the overall CDG experience 

Bring an officer-centric perspective to CDGO’s work, continually asking how policies, programmes and communications come together from an officer’s point of view. 

Identify gaps or disconnects in the way officers encounter CDG and work with relevant teams to improve the experience. 

Explore new ways of making CDG easier to understand and act on, including through better content, communications, design and digital approaches. 

Work across organisational boundaries to build greater coherence between policy intent, programme implementation and officers’ lived experience of CDG.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone who is a strong storyteller and systems thinker — someone who can see the connections across multiple initiatives and turn them into a simple, compelling narrative. You should be comfortable working in an environment where the story is still evolving. You will need to understand the substance behind different policies and programmes, identify what matters to officers, and work with communications professionals and policy teams to translate this into something meaningful and actionable. 


You should have: 

Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly the ability to make policy or technical concepts accessible and relevant. 

Some experience in strategic communications and storytelling, with the ability to turn complex and fragmented information into a coherent narrative. 

Strong synthesis and conceptual thinking skills, with the ability to see connections across different policies, programmes and initiatives. 

Good stakeholder management and collaboration skills, particularly when working across teams with different objectives and areas of expertise. 

Good judgement and sensitivity to organisational context. 

An experimental mindset and willingness to test different ways of communicating and engaging officers. 

Experience in strategic communications, employee communications, change communications, policy, organisational development, employee experience or related work would be advantageous. 


Our Core Competencies 

The role will draw particularly strongly on OCCs relating to: 

Thinking clearly and making sound judgements — making sense of multiple policies, programmes and perspectives and identifying the underlying story that connects them. 

Working as One Public Service — working across PSD teams to build a coherent CDG experience. 

Improving and innovating continuously — experimenting with different ways of making CDG tangible and relevant, and refining approaches based on how officers respond. 

Keep learning and putting skills into action — understanding officers’ needs and experiences and applying those insights to improve how CDG is communicated and experienced.
