DECODING THE WORLD FOR SINGAPORE’S DECISION MAKERS

Do you often ask why countries behave in a certain way? Curious about why global trends play out the way they do? Are you passionate about helping Singapore secure its place in the world?

At Security and Intelligence Division (SID), you are a key source of expertise and insight into geopolitics and international security within the Singapore government. We analyse and synthesise myriad information into insights that directly inform national leaders and top policymakers. Join us in decoding a dynamic and uncertain world for Singapore’s top decision-makers.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Build and Maintain Strategic Awareness: monitor and sieve through information to find, verify, and interpret data and information from multiple sources
•	Forecast Trends and Emerging Risks which impacting Singapore’s national interests
•	Provide Timely and Relevant Insights for national leaders and top policymakers in the form of policy briefings and high-impact writing
•	Conduct Deep Research into specific countries/regions, and/or multilateral trends and themes
•	Engage Key Policymaking Agencies in the Singapore government: brief key decision-makers on critical issues and participate in cross-agency discussions as subject matter experts, while also gaining a better understanding of national interests
•	Build Partnerships: engage foreign government partners as part of intelligence diplomacy, and to sharpen analysis, deepen expertise, and build intelligence tradecraft
•	At senior levels: 
        - Lead and manage teams of analysts
        - Develop cognitive tools and methods to ensure robust and insightful analysis 
        - Develop junior analysts

What you will gain:

•	High-Level Impact, Direct Executive Visibility: produce insights that go straight to the desks of top policymakers shaping Singapore's national strategy
•	High-Calibre Teams: be part of a community of passionate geopol geeks and country specialists in an intellectually stimulating environment
•	Access to top thinkers in governments and academia on critical and emerging global issues
•	Culture of Continuous Learning: we invest heavily in professional training, such as in-house training, collaborative training with foreign partners, and access to courses by local universities
jobRequirements:
•     Singapore Citizens only

We value intellectual curiosity and an openness to alternative ideas; critical thinking and evidence-based analytical skills; and a drive for excellence. A good command of English and some comfort with uncertainty and ambiguity are also necessary. If you love dissecting complex international issues and explaining why it matters for Singapore in simple terms, you’ll fit right in.

We will provide the tradecraft training; you bring the curiosity. Your job isn’t to know all the answers today, but to have the drive to uncover them. Desired qualities and attributes include:
•	Keen interest in geopolitical, threat or security-related developments
•	Strong written and verbal communication skills
•	Detail-oriented but also able to see the big picture
•	Able and willing to learn
•	Strong interpersonal skills and able to work collaboratively
•	Motivated and independent
•	Strong problem-solving skills

agencyDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD) stewards a trusted Singapore Public Service for a successful and vibrant Singapore. Our 4 key roles include:
•	Developing a flourishing and diverse workforce by supporting our public officers' continual growth of skills and creating meaningful careers 
•	Developing a forward-looking and inspiring community of leaders who are united, resilient, and anchored in public service values and ethos
•	Building future-ready public sector organisations by steering and supporting transformation of our organisations and catalysing innovations for organisations to work more effectively
•	Driving good governance, values and excellence to safeguard the integrity and reputation of the Public Service and uphold the trust of citizens 

Why Join Us
When you join PSD, you become part of a community that learns together and cares for one another. We look out for your well-being and partner you in your career growth. Being in the business of developing People and driving transformation makes our work deeply Purposeful. What you do will impact our public officers and agencies, and in turn make a difference to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you share our passion in reimagining Possibilities and pushing boundaries to shape a first-class Public Service, we welcome you to join us!

jobDescription:
The Singapore Public Service offers an attractive career proposition for those who seek to make a difference in service of Singapore and Singaporeans. 

To navigate a more complex and fast-changing environment, the Public Service needs a diversity of strengths and perspectives in our leadership ranks. We therefore welcome leaders with different backgrounds, who wish to contribute their skills and perspectives in the Public Service to make a meaningful impact to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you take up a public service leadership career, we will invest in your development so that you can lead effectively in the Public Service, for today and tomorrow. A key feature of pursuing a public service leadership career is the opportunity for you to undergo structured job postings across different public agencies, to expose you to critical job experiences and key issues facing Government.
jobResponsibilities:
Here are some areas you could contribute to, across the key sectors of Government:

• Social: Shape the ‘heartware’ of Singapore – cultivating a more cohesive, resilient, caring and inclusive society.

• Economy Building: Contribute to Singapore’s growth, macro-economic stability, industry regulation and a conducive business environment.

• Infrastructure & Environment: Contribute to making Singapore a vibrant, clean, liveable city with sustainable development, robust infrastructure and good connectivity.

• Security: Keep Singapore safe and secure through robust enforcement capabilities and sound security policies.

• Central Administration: Ensure effective and efficient use of resources and help develop a consultative and customer-centric Public Service.

• Info-Comm Technology & Smart Systems: Enable better use of data and harnessing of new technologies by the Government to build a digital economy and digital society, in support of Smart Nation.
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be one who: 

• Believes in and demonstrates the Public Service Values of Integrity, Service, Excellence.
• Has the passion to serve and a commitment towards building a better Singapore and to improve the lives of current and future generations of Singaporeans.
• Demonstrates strong leadership qualities, interpersonal skills and cognitive thinking capacities. More senior candidates should have a strong track record in demonstrating these key areas through past work experiences.
• Is a Singapore Citizen.

*Note: The above application route is for candidates who are not currently serving in the Public Service. If you are a public officer, you should contact your Ministry/Agency HR team for more details.

For new graduates, or individuals with around 1 year of working experience, you can look forward to a structured development programme on the PSLP General Phase (GP) that will expose you to the key job roles in the Public Service (i.e. across roles in policy, operations, stakeholder management). This will support your foundational development as a young leader. You will also get to experience work in at least 2 sectors to support you in understanding your longer-term career preferences and aspirations.  

You can obtain updates on the status of your application through the same portal. For shortlisted candidates, PSD will contact you to provide details of the selection process. 
 
• Information on the PSLP and PSC Master’s Scholarship •

For more information on the PSLP, please visit https://www.psd.gov.sg/leadership/public-service-leadership-careers for further clarification.

You may also find out more details of the PSC Master’s Scholarship at https://www.scholarships.gov.sg.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Department of Statistics is the National Statistical Authority responsible for statistics on the Singapore economy and population.

We collect, compile, analyse and disseminate a wide range of economic, business, household and population data, as well as analyse and monitor trends in the economy and population.

With these vital inputs, policymakers, business decision makers and our data users gain valuable insights into current and emerging economic and social trends, enabling them to make calculated and informed decisions in the formulation of policies and strategies for the future. Apart from public agencies and businesses, our users also include researchers, analysts, educators, students, the media and the general public.

Join our team and make a difference by contributing important statistical input to facilitate policy planning and decision-making and support Singapore's present and future economic and social development.
jobDescription: As a Statistician, you will be responsible for the data gathering and compilation of statistics in one or more specific fields, conduct statistical research and analysis, and develop new systems and indicators to support users' statistical requirements.
jobResponsibilities: You will also be involved in managing, analysing and making sense of large amounts of data from various sources, to optimise statistical processes and derive more insights from the data to support policy-making.

• Possess knowledge or experience in Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, Accountancy, Actuarial Science and/or subjects with substantial quantitative content (e.g., regression, analytics, modelling, forecasting)
• Strong analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to learn and apply relevant statistical and analytical tools and techniques for data compilation and analysis
• Good communication and presentation skills
• Able to work well both independently and as a member of a team

This job advertisement does not have a fixed closing date as DOS recruits Statistician on a year-round basis.

Development Opportunities and Benefits:  

•	DOS believes in the career development and training of our staff to bring out their best potential at work 
•	You will be equipped with skills and subject matter know-how via in-house and external learning and development opportunities. You will also be exposed to different statistical work via our structured job rotation programme. 
•	DOS offers attractive and market competitive benefits which include mid-year & year-end variable payments and market adjustment component. 
•	To support your personal needs, DOS also provides for flexible working arrangements including hybrid work and staggered working hours.

jobDescription: Foreign Service Officers (FSOs) serve as Singapore’s diplomats to safeguard and protect our fellow countrymen and advance Singapore’s interests abroad. As an FSO, you must be prepared for a career that alternates between deployments to MFA HQ and to any of our over 50 embassies, high commissions and consulates around the world. Applicants may pursue a career with MFA as an FSO on either the Political & Economic track, or the Functional & Corporate track.
jobResponsibilities:
As an FSO (Functional & Corporate) in HQ, you will formulate, review and implement policies that impact MFA's vital operations in the core functions such as: Consular, Protocol, Human Resource, Corporate Affairs and Development Partnerships.

jobRequirements:
To meet the challenges of this role, you must have/be

•	Singaporean
•	A keen interest in international affairs
•	Versatile and adaptable to different environments
•	Strong analytical skills and conceptual abilities
•	Excellent written and oral communication skills
•	Strong ability to engage people at all levels
•	Good planning and organisation skills
•	Creative problem-solvers who are able to think on their feet
•	Open to relocation overseas

You will be working in a fast-paced and highly volatile environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.

Graduates (with or without experience) from all disciplines may apply. Salary will commensurate with experience.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The selection process consists of three successive stages. Candidates who pass each stage will be notified via email to proceed to the next stage. Please contact mfa_career@mfa.gov.sg if you require assistance with your application.

The Fair Consideration Framework sets out requirements for employers to consider the workforce in Singapore fairly for job opportunities. Given the complex and rapidly-evolving security terrain, your work will be fast-paced, challenging and stimulating.

You will be part of HPB’s Research, Evaluation and Monitoring (REM) division, which drives the development of data-driven insights and analytics to inform health promotion strategies across HPB. The division focuses on translating cutting-edge research and emerging technologies into HPB programmes. By distilling learnings from diverse datasets, applied research, and innovative pilots, REM supports the translation of evidence into practice for delivery in national-scale platforms. You will generate actionable insights through advanced analytics on diverse datasets (e.g. large longitudinal cohorts, sensors, and combined datasets), applying appropriate statistical and machine learning approaches to support risk prediction, population segmentation, and identification of behavioural patterns.

You will support the development and application of predictive models and segmentation approaches (e.g. clustering) to inform programme targeting, intervention design, and risk stratification, ensuring outputs are robust, interpretable, and relevant for real-world decision-making.

You will set up and support behavioural experiments and programme evaluations, including contributing to study design, data preparation, and analysis to distil research insights and evaluate suitability for translation into programme delivery.

You will develop compelling data-driven narratives for impactful storytelling to both internal and external stakeholders, translating technical findings into clear, concise, and actionable insights that inform programme and policy decisions.

You will work with cross-functional teams and external partners to support collaborations and analytics projects, contributing to delivery of strategic outcomes and facilitating knowledge sharing and learning across teams.

You will support the development of data pipelines, feature engineering, and preparation of datasets to enable efficient and scalable analytics, including working with relevant data platforms where required.

The ideal candidate will be a dynamic and self-motivated individual with a strong interest in advancing health promotion through data, research, and analytics.   • At least 2–6 years of practical experience working with data as an analyst or in a related role

jobDescription:

Energy is an existential issue for Singapore. We import almost all our energy supply and are exposed to global energy market movements. Recent global developments and energy crises have disrupted the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they manage rising energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. At the same time, our energy system is an enabler for economic growth, as speed to power is critical to capture strategic and economically significant investments.

Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost-competitive energy system that safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism.
jobResponsibilities:
METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships.

The Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in ensuring energy remains a key enabler of Singapore’s competitiveness, climate goals and national resilience via the five ‘Cs’:

•	Confidence - ensure our system resilience continues to be a source of confidence for our people, through multiple lines of defence to safeguard energy security, resilience, and reliability. These include diversifying our fuel sources and strengthening our fuel reserves.

•	Competitiveness - harness energy to bolster our economic competitiveness, through scaling our generation and grid capacity to meet growing needs and attract electricity-intensive investments. This also involves reviewing our energy system planning models and leveraging flexibility assets to secure speed to power while maintaining system reliability.

•	Carbon - ensure our power system infrastructure and electricity market are ready for a low-carbon future to meet our climate commitments. Infrastructure and markets are critical to ensuring Singapore can pursue every possible pathway to develop a diversified and affordable portfolio of low-carbon energy options.

•	Connectivity - deepen connectivity with our partners and ensure new imported energy sources can enter Singapore’s grid and electricity market.

•	Costs - keep costs in check to ensure we strike the right balance in the energy transition. This involves right-pricing energy and infrastructure, and ensuring our market frameworks continue to support a competitive and commercially sustainable generation sector.'

•	Formulate robust strategies and policies to regulate and develop the gas and electricity sectors. •	Formulate and review policies and strategies to develop supporting enablers for the electricity and gas sectors, including infrastructure and financing.

•	Monitor developments in global energy markets and analyse implications for domestic energy policies.

Advance the data-driven, evidence-based and citizen-centric approach to health promotion through state-of-the-art data best practices to maximize data quality and internationally-recognised governance and policies to promote safe usage of data.

Overview of Data Operations & Architecture Department

Recognising the efficacy of big data and artificial intelligence in optimising sharper insights and outcomes for public health, the Data Operations and Architecture Department will take a proactive role to drive the design of a 360-view citizen-centric data architecture and the implementation of data operations to support and facilitate an evidence-based, data-driven approach to programme delivery. You will be pivotal in helping to set up and implement a robust data engineering pipeline that can integrate the vast wealth of data HPB has through its numerous data sources. A robust data pipeline ensures that changes from the data sources does not impact the timely delivery of high quality data to our business users.

Given the diversity of data collected from our lifestyle programmes, data science approaches such as machine learning will also be deployed to support the data engineering process. For example, we have build and included machine learning ops to help with standardising event names.

  • Translate research and analytics questions into data features to facilitate dashboarding, model training, analytics, and data science applications

jobDescription: PRINCIPAL / SENIOR / EXECUTIVE CYBERSECURITY ENGINEER, AV CYBERSECURITY
jobResponsibilities:
Centre for Autonomous Mobility (CAM) leads Singapore’s national effort to deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) at scale. As AVs move onto public roads, their cybersecurity becomes a matter of public safety: a compromised vehicle is not just a data breach but a physical risk. You will be part of the cybersecurity team responsible for developing the cybersecurity assurance regime for AVs, to ensure autonomous vehicles are deployed safely and securely in Singapore. You will drive to grow into AV cybersecurity. You will help build the function from the ground up assuring the cybersecurity of AVs themselves, and securing the systems CAM builds to oversee them.

Your responsibilities:

● Drive the development of the regulatory framework for AVs, such as establishing requirements for a Cyber Security Management System (CSMS) that covers the vehicle’s lifecycle — development, production and deployment.

● Assess AV developers’ cybersecurity submissions against our assurance criteria, applying Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment (TARA) and the R155 Annex 5 threats and controls, as well as standards such as ISO/SAE 21434.

● Define expectations for secure over-the-air software updates in line with the intent of UN R156 (a Software Update Management System), and for managing cyber risk across the AV supply chain.

● Establish monitoring, detection and incident response requirements for AVs, including analysing threats, vulnerabilities and mitigations to contribute to collective knowledge for the AV ecosystem.

● Maintain the policies, standards and playbooks for AV cybersecurity, and support engagement with local partners and international fora (e.g. UNECE WP.29 / GRVA).

Help secure CAM’s digital products / DevSecOps (secondary)

The other part of the team’s remit is making sure the systems CAM builds to regulate and monitor AVs — such as the Autonomous Vehicle Monitoring System — are themselves secure by design.

● Work with the Systems team to build security into the software development lifecycle, from design through CI/CD to production.

● Conduct security architecture and design reviews and risk assessments of CAM’s systems, and provide and implement remediation recommendations.

● Support security reviews of application code and architecture, and help design secure-by-default components.

● Set up automated security testing — SAST/DAST, dependency and secrets scanning, and infrastructure-as-code checks — in the delivery pipeline.

● Assist with breach detection and incident response for these products.

Help build the function

● As you grow into the role, you will naturally spot gaps and suggest tools, processes and improvements as the team and its remit grow.

● Evaluate emerging security technologies and recommend tools and approaches for the team to adopt.

● Provide security advice to CAM project teams on design and architecture decisions, and help build a security-minded culture across CAM, working alongside engineers, AV developers and agency partners.

For more senior hire, you will:

● Own and drive the AV cybersecurity assurance framework end to end, and set the assurance criteria AV developers must meet.

● Lead assessments of AV developers’ cybersecurity management systems and act as a technical authority in deployment-approval decisions on cybersecurity assurance adequacy.

● Help establish security architecture governance and compliance with relevant frameworks.

● Lead cybersecurity incident response for the AV fleet and our products, and define the team’s tooling, standards and processes.

● Mentor junior engineers and help grow the team.
jobRequirements:
● Knowledge preferably in Computer Science, Cybersecurity or a related field

● Thinks analytically about risk — can reason about threats, weigh trade-offs, and understand the limits of a cybersecurity control on safety outcomes.

● Eager to learn vehicle regulations — genuinely interested in standards and frameworks like R155, and able to pick them up quickly.

● Communicates clearly — can explain security issues to both technical and non-technical people.

● Takes initiative and cares about the public good — this is new ground, so you will help shape the standards rather than inherit them.

● Familiarity with automotive / vehicle cybersecurity standards and regulation — UN R155 and R156, ISO/SAE 21434, CSMS and TARA — or a track record of picking up new regulatory frameworks quickly.

● Exposure to automotive, operational-technology (OT) or embedded / safety-critical systems security, including security architecture of cloud-native applications and/or OT systems.

● Hands-on DevSecOps experience: secure SDLC, CI/CD pipeline security, cloud security (e.g. AWS), and SAST/DAST tooling.

● Hands-on experience with security tools such as SIEM, WAF, IPS, privileged access management (PAM), or data loss prevention (DLP).

● Professional accreditations such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, GICSP, GCIH or OSCP.

● A strong interest in autonomous vehicles, emerging mobility technology and overall vehicular safety.

AI systems are only as good as the data that powers them. As a Data Engineer in LTA's Transport AI Programme, you will design, build, and maintain the data infrastructure and pipelines that enable AI models and applications to access high-quality, timely, and trustworthy data. You will work across LTA's rich transport data ecosystem — spanning real-time sensor feeds, transit operations data, traffic systems, and road infrastructure — to ensure that data is reliably ingested, transformed, governed, and made available for AI development and production use.

This role reports to the Transport AI Programme Deputy Director and works closely with AI software developers, the AI architect, infrastructure engineers, and industry partners on joint data integration efforts.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain scalable data pipelines that ingest, transform, and serve structured and unstructured data from diverse transport data sources, including real-time streams and batch feeds.

  • Ensure data quality, consistency, and lineage across the data platform, implementing validation checks, monitoring, and alerting to detect and resolve data issues early.

  • Implement data governance practices in line with Singapore Government data classification requirements, including access controls, data masking, anonymisation, and audit logging for sensitive transport and personal data.

  • Work with the AI Architect and Infrastructure Engineer to design data infrastructure that is performant, cost-efficient, and aligned with LTA's cloud and hybrid environment.

  • Collaborate with data scientists and AI developers to understand data requirements for model development, and translate these into reliable, production-grade data products.

  • Support the integration of external data sources from industry partners, ensuring that data exchange meets LTA's standards for security, quality, and interoperability.

  • Contribute to the development of shared data platforms and reusable data assets that can be leveraged across multiple AI use cases within the programme.

As an Engineer, you may be deployed to one of PUB’s five Operations Departments or other departments based on organisational needs, to manage and develop Singapore’s water resources:

As part of the Catchment & Waterways (C&W) Department, you will be part of a team that plans, develops and manages our reservoirs and waterways for water supply and flood control, and integrate them with the surrounding environment in a sustainable manner.

2. Water Supply (Plants)

The Water Supply Plants (WSP) Department aims to provide an adequate and reliable supply of potable water at the most economical cost, and to operate and maintain Water Treatment Plants and Desalination Plants to produce safe drinking water to meet daily demands.

3. Water Supply (Network)

The Water Supply Network (WSN) Department plays a key role in delivering good water to businesses and end-users 24/7 – to ensure reliable and good quality supply to customers, and to manage and keep water demand low. This is done through various ways such as network optimisation, maintenance and renewal, as well as network planning and data management.

4. Water Reclamation (Plants)

The Water Reclamation Plants (WRP) Department is responsible for the treatment of all used water to a quality suitable for the production of NEWater or Industrial Water, and for safe discharge to the sea. Officers may be deployed to one of PUB’s Water Reclamation Plants in Jurong, Ulu Pandan, Kranji or Changi, or NEWater Factories in Bedok or Kranji.

5. Water Reclamation (Network)

The Water Reclamation Network (WRN) Department aims to collect and convey all used water for reclamation cost effectively and reliably. This is done through three key functions – Planning & Design of Sewerage Infrastructures; Network Operation and Maintenance; and Project management.

jobDescription: SENIOR/ MANAGER, DATA PARTNERSHIPS — TRANSPORT AI PROGRAMME, LTA SINGAPORE
jobResponsibilities:
Singapore's land transport network moves millions of people every day. As AI reshapes what's possible in transport operations, the Land Transport Authority is investing in AI capabilities that will meaningfully improve how the network is sensed, managed, and optimised — for commuters, operators, and public officers alike.

AI systems are only as good as the data that powers them. We are looking for a Senior/ Manager to establish and lead our data acquisition and partnership function — the foundational capability that will enable our organisation to develop meaningful, operationally relevant data use cases and AI-enabled applications.

Beyond internal organisational data, operationally relevant datasets may be found across government agencies, industry partners, and contractors — each governed by their own access controls, sharing frameworks, and institutional considerations. You will be required to understand our concept of operations well enough to determine what data is needed, and pursue access to that data through establishing relationships, agreements and organisational infrastructure required to bring the right data in securely and sustainably.

What You Will Be Working On

You will lead a team to translate our concept of operations into a prioritised multi-modal data acquisition roadmap, identifying what data we need and sequencing efforts by operational value and feasibility. Your work also involves stakeholder engagement, negotiating access with government agencies, statutory boards, industries and research institutions.

As part of data acquisition, you will lead your team to define and enforce standards for how data is received — covering file formats, data schemas, metadata requirements, and update cadences. This ensures that datasets from disparate sources can be reliably ingested, integrated, and made ready for analytical and AI workloads. Where partners or contractors are unable to meet these standards natively, you will work with them to find practical solutions or manage the necessary transformation processes internally.

You will also be responsible for identifying and building the right platform for consolidating data from multiple sources, particularly where contractor or sensitive datasets introduce security and classification constraints that may rule out standard environments. You will work with technical, legal, and cybersecurity colleagues to arrive at an appropriate approach.

Underpinning all of this is sound data governance — ensuring that what we acquire is handled compliantly, with appropriate agreements and access controls in place. You will work closely with analytical, AI development and product teams to ensure that acquired data is properly onboarded and ready for use case development.

You will be part of the Risk Assurance Division within IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group. The Holistic Assessment team in this Division assesses the overall cybersecurity risk posture of critical digital networks and systems and the cyber capabilities of organisations operating these networks.

This includes integrating diverse sources of information, across the organisation’s external environment, its internal capabilities and the performance of its networks and systems. The team adopts an evidence-based approach to develop an objective assessment of the organisation and network’s key strengths and vulnerabilities. It also recommends key areas that senior management should track to uplift its cybersecurity risk posture.

The Holistic Assessment team works with teams across IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group, and in partnership with industry stakeholders. It regularly engages senior management in both IMDA and the industry, to review its findings and recommendations. Through these, the Holistic Assessment team plays a critical role in ensuring that the critical digital networks and systems which underpin Singapore’s Digital Economy remain secure and resilient.

  • Conduct research and sense making of the evolving cybersecurity landscape in relation to Singapore’s digital infrastructure. This includes integrating threat intelligence information as well as international industry best practices for defending against current and emerging cyber threats.

  • Design technical tests to validate the effectiveness of cybersecurity measures within these priority areas. The Southeast Asia and Oceania Division (SEAO) is a division in the Singapore Economic Development Board. SEAO plays a critical role in strengthening linkages between Singapore and the immediate region, and expanding Singapore’s economic hinterland. SEAO (i) develops and executes on government-to-government (G2G) partnerships; (ii) actively engages the region’s top private sector players – including major conglomerates, sectoral champions, and high growth startups, and (iii) facilitates the growth of global MNCs in Southeast Asia via Singapore. As a Manager/Senior Manager in the SEAO Division, you will operate at the unique intersection of bilateral economic policy, inter-agency stakeholder engagement, and investment promotion. You will have operational oversight over core cross-border economic initiatives, and support EDB’s corporate engagement in key regional markets including Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. You will work with both global MNCs and regional conglomerates to best harness Singapore’s strengths and the complementary advantages of our immediate neighbours. You will need to understand and assess Singapore’s strategic interests, needs and develop the right solutions catered to Singapore’s position as a global business centre. You will also cultivate and maintain close ties with key influencers or decision makers in Singapore and the region ranging from government officials, industry leaders and company executives.

  • Drive Cross-Border Initiatives: Lead the operationalization and policy coordination for Singapore’s key regional partnerships, specifically the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and Batam-Bintan-Karimun region (BBK).

  • Inter-Agency Stakeholder Engagement: Work across multiple Singapore Government stakeholders to balance various interests and develop win-win solutions.

  • Bilateral Diplomacy: Work closely with bilateral government counterparts to align economic priorities, address cross-border regulatory frictions, and attract new investments into the region.

Corporate Account Management & Market Strategy

  • Portfolio Account Management: Support the management and engagement of strategic corporate relationships in Malaysia and the Philippines.

  • Engagement of key executives: Cultivate trusted relationships with senior company executives and next-generation business leaders to understand their regional expansion roadmaps and long-term priorities.

  • At least 3 to 5 years of relevant working experience in corporate strategy, investment promotion, management consulting, public policy, or international trade relations.

  • Deep Regional Context: Strong understanding of the Southeast Asian macroeconomic landscape, with specific familiarity regarding the corporate governance, regulatory environments, and market dynamics of Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

Its key roles are to improve and sustain a clean environment, promote sustainability and resource efficiency, maintain high public health standards, provide timely and reliable meteorological information, and encourage a vibrant hawker culture. NEA works closely with its partners and the community to develop and spearhead environmental and public health initiatives and programmes. It is committed to motivating every individual to care for the environment as a way of life, in order to build a liveable and sustainable Singapore for present and future generations.

For more information, visit www.nea.gov.sg
jobDescription: The Workplace Safety and Health Division (WSHD) is a corporate function responsible for driving workplace safety and health excellence across NEA. We provide central oversight of WSH culture, governance, capabilities and compliance, and work closely with NEA’s leadership, WSH Committees, Safety Offices and Divisions to strengthen risk management, enhance organisational capabilities, and foster a strong safety culture.
jobResponsibilities:
As the Executive Manager, WSH Audit & Compliance Branch, you will plan and implement the organisation's Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) assurance programme by providing independent Line 2 oversight, strengthening Line 1 capability, and driving continuous improvement by leveraging technology and data to enhance organisational WSH performance.

  • Plan and implement the organisation's Line 2 WSH assurance programme by conducting risk-based audits and inspections to evaluate the effectiveness of WSH management systems and critical controls across Tier 1 and Tier 2 business groups.

  • Strengthen organisational WSH governance and capability by guiding Line 1 in the planning and execution of audits and inspections, and developing resources and engagement initiatives to enhance frontline assurance and root-cause analysis.

  • Provide strategic oversight and insights by analysing audit and inspection outcomes, identifying systemic risks and trends, and presenting analysis and recommendations to support Senior Management oversight and informed management decision-making. This includes developing a comprehensive WSH dashboard to provide real-time visibility into key safety metrics and performance indicators.

  • Develop, implement and review WSH manuals and procedures, and provide expert WSH advisory and governance support to business units on WSH management systems, regulatory requirements and best practices to drive continual improvement in WSH performance.

  • Drive innovation and digital transformation by identifying opportunities to adopt WSH technologies, evaluating use cases, and leading pilot initiatives to enhance assurance and operational performance.

  • Manage strategic partnerships with external consultants and internal stakeholders to strengthen organisational assurance capability and continuously improve WSH governance frameworks and practices.
jobRequirements:
Requirements:

  • Good knowledge of the Singapore Workplace Safety and Health (WSH), Environmental Protection and Fire Safety Act, subsidiary legislations, relevant Codes of Practice and Singapore Standards, as well as WSH management systems and governance frameworks.
  • Has at least 5 years of relevant work experience, preferably in WSH management, audit and assurance, risk management, compliance, governance, or related functions.
  • Experience in planning or conducting WSH audits, inspections or assurance activities, and analysing findings to identify systemic risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Experience in stakeholder engagement, capability development or project management will be an advantage.
  • Registered WSH Officer (WSHO), ISO 45001 Auditor/Lead Auditor, or Specialist Diploma in WSH (or equivalent) will have an added advantage.
  • Strong analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data and findings into strategic insights and practical recommendations.
  • Excellent writing, communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organisation.
  • Organised, adaptable and able to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.
  • Mature, resourceful and able to work independently while building effective partnerships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Self-driven with a continuous improvement mindset and a keen interest in leveraging technology and innovation to enhance WSH performance.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

Applicants will be updated on the status of their applications within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

jobDescription:
The Procurement Function reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). The Assistant Director, Procurement plays a strategic leadership role in driving procurement excellence across the organisation. The incumbent will lead the development and execution of procurement strategies that deliver value, strengthen governance, optimise spending, mitigate risks, and ensure business continuity.

As a key member of the Procurement team, you will provide leadership and direction in:

• Strategic sourcing and category management
• Procurement policy, governance and compliance
• Contract and supplier relationship management
• Stakeholder engagement and business partnering
• Procurement transformation and digitalisation
• Procurement operations and continuous improvement

The role requires strong analytical capabilities, sound judgement, stakeholder influence, and the ability to translate business needs into effective procurement solutions that support organisational objectives.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic Sourcing and Category Management

  • Lead the development and implementation of sourcing strategies for assigned spend categories to achieve value-for-money outcomes, operational efficiencies, and sustainable cost savings.

  • Partner stakeholders to optimise requirements and specifications while leveraging HPB's overall purchasing power.

  • Monitor market conditions, industry trends, and supply risks to ensure continuity of essential services and critical supplies.

  • Drive procurement planning and demand management initiatives to strengthen procurement outcomes.

Business Partnering and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders by providing clear, practical, and consistent procurement guidance throughout the procurement lifecycle.

  • Influence and engage stakeholders to make informed sourcing decisions and adopt best procurement practices.

  • Champion a value-driven procurement culture by repositioning procurement from a reactive function to a strategic business partner.

Governance, Risk and Compliance

  • Develop, review, and strengthen procurement policies, frameworks, and governance processes to ensure compliance with Government procurement requirements and organisational policies.

  • Review and assess procurement strategies, evaluation outcomes, and award recommendations before submission for approval.

  • Identify procurement and contract-related risks, establish key risk indicators, and implement appropriate mitigation measures.

  • Ensure transparency, accountability, and good governance across procurement activities.

Contract and Supplier Management

  • Foster strategic supplier relationships to obtain market intelligence, industry insights, emerging innovations, and leading practices.

  • Drive supplier performance management and contract governance to maximise contract value and minimise operational risks.

  • Analyse critical contract failure points and implement proactive measures to enhance contract performance and service delivery.

Procurement Transformation and Analytics

  • Leverage data analytics and market intelligence to support decision-making, develop sourcing strategies, and maximise return on investment.

  • Identify opportunities to streamline procurement processes, enhance efficiency, and improve user experience through digitalisation and automation.

  • Support procurement transformation initiatives and continuous improvement programmes across the organisation.
jobRequirements:
Qualifications and Experience

  • At least 8 years of relevant procurement, purchasing, sourcing, or supply chain management experience, with demonstrated experience in leading strategic procurement initiatives in public sector and/or commercial sector.

  • Professional procurement certification such as CPM, CPSM, MCIPS, or equivalent will be an advantage.

  • Experience in managing eSourcing platforms and digital procurement solutions.

Technical Competencies

  • Strong expertise in strategic sourcing, category management, contract management, supplier relationship management, and procurement governance.

  • Advanced knowledge of procurement risk management and supplier evaluation methodologies.

  • Proven ability to develop procurement policies, frameworks, and operating procedures.

Leadership and Behavioural Competencies

  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to engage effectively across all organisational levels.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to navigate ambiguity, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.

  • Strategic thinker with strong commercial acumen and sound judgement.

  • Proactive, resilient, and results-oriented with a passion for driving procurement excellence and organisational value.

Key Success Factors

  • The successful candidate will be a strategic procurement leader who can balance governance with business needs, influence stakeholders effectively, leverage data-driven insights, and drive procurement transformation while delivering measurable value to the organisation.

  • Strong analytical and data interpretation skills with the ability to translate insights into actionable procurement strategies.

  • Good knowledge of Government Procurement Instructions Manual (GPIM), GeBIZ, and related procurement systems will be advantageous.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract in the first instance.

jobTitle: Manager/ Assistant Manager (Programme Architects), YCS [3-year contract]
agencyDescription:

jobDescription:
Be part of Youth Corps Singapore!
A division of the National Youth Council, Youth Corps Singapore (YCS) champions youth volunteerism nationwide in Singapore, empowering and supporting young Singaporeans to ignite positive change and make impactful difference in society. We are a national movement of young people with strong espirit de corps and service ethos, harnessing the optimism of young people, the passion of community partners and the transformative power of service learning to serve and build cohesive and inclusive communities.

Join us to ignite positive change!
YCS is seeking dynamic individuals to be part of the team to champion youth volunteerism in the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHL). The team builds the capabilities of youth leaders to design and lead impactful community service projects, curates meaningful volunteering experiences for their peers, ignites the spark for volunteerism in more youths, and grows the national youth volunteerism movement. The team also builds the larger Youth Corps Singapore eco-system and communities of practice, connecting youth leaders to networks and resources to sustain and create multipliers for their volunteerism efforts.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Programmes Design and Coordination - Oversee the design and content creation for Youth Corps programmes, whichever includes programme administration, planning and conducting activities and events to engage youth, as well as introducing them to the larger Youth Corps ecosystem. The candidate should also be able to advise on the use of training theories and tools (e.g. simulations, facilitation, role-play, volunteering framework etc.) for Youth Corps training modules.
•	Training Programme Design, Coordination and Delivery - Develop, deliver and/or coordinate with training partners to design and implement skills development workshops aligned with Youth Corps objectives, for youths. 
•	Programme and Training Evaluation - Provide and analyse evaluative feedback on the programme and training to assess the effectiveness, with the overall objective of equipping the youths with the necessary skills to create sustainable community impact and sustaining their volunteerism beyond the programme.
•	Evaluation Data Management - Manage the process of survey data collection and curate survey questions based on NYC key indicator outcomes. Guide team members in effective data collection and analysis practices.	
•	School Partners Engagement - Support and provide consultation to the schools in their engagement with community partners, stakeholders, and key resources in the sector as support for their service projects. Identify learning needs in collaboration with IHL partners to design and coordinate training programmes tailored for youth development.
•	Community Partner Engagement - Collaborate with community partners to curate meaningful service opportunities suitable for youth volunteers that are impactful and sustainable in the community. 
•	Project Consultation - Provide consultation and mentor the youths in the design and delivery of their service project to create sustainable and impactful community service projects, ensuring alignment with community needs.
jobRequirements:
•	Background and/or strong interest in community service, youth development, programme coordination, training and/or partners management
•	Experience in partnership management with Social Service Agencies and IHLs
•	Possess excellent communication and writing skills for development of training curriculum
•	Competent in designing, facilitating and delivering training programmes with interactive and effective learning activities
•	Ability to mentor and engage youth volunteers, including availability during weekday evenings and weekends
•	Ability to adapt well and thrive in a dynamic environment with attributes of proactiveness, resourcefulness, self-motivation, curiosity and learning agility
•	Proactive team player with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to thrive in cross-functional teams within a dynamic environment
•	Relevant experiences will be advantageous: Manager (1 to 3 years)

agencyDescription:
The Skills and Workforce Development Agency (SWDA), a statutory board under the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), drives lifelong learning and workforce development to enable Singaporeans to take charge of their careers, learn for life, access good jobs, and grow in fulfilling careers. We enable employers to build a skilled, future-ready workforce, design quality jobs, and adopt skills recognition practices. Together with our partners, we build a trusted, high-quality, industry-relevant, and innovative ecosystem that meets the evolving workforce needs of both businesses and workers.   

Guided by our vision of a Singapore where everyone can grow in fulfilling careers, we live our promise of Building Skills, Growing Careers by nurturing lifelong learning, strengthening employability and enabling career growth for all, including our own officers, through a continuous learning culture and a supportive, flexible, inclusive working environment that fosters innovation, collaboration, and well-being.

So, join us to be part of a dynamic team driving the national SkillsFuture movement and building a strong Singaporean core. Together, we create opportunities, transform lives, and shape the future of work.

This includes:

  • Strong writing and communication skills: Able to actively participate in discussions with stakeholders and translate perspectives into sound recommendations (in both writing and presentations) for management’s consideration.

Relevant experience in strategic planning, policy, programme management, corporate planning or related areas.

Knowledge/ Skills

  • Good understanding of labour market, workforce transformation trends, including the impact of technology and automation.

  • Awareness of government initiatives relating to manpower, workforce development and human capital would be advantageous.

Abilities/Aptitudes:

  • Strong analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

  • Proactive, with a strong sense of ownership and follow-through.

jobDescription:

This involves contract management on long-term term contractors and OEMs to ensure KPIs compliance, driving data-led predictive maintenance and managing overhaul and system upgrade projects.

Additionally, the role handles incident investigations and root cause analyses, while championing knowledge management. The ultimate goal is to guarantee system safety, reliability and service excellence to deliver a positive guest experience for all stakeholders.

  • Supervise and ensure planned preventive and corrective maintenance is carried out by term contractor in accordance with the checklists, specifications & requirements of the contract, relevant authority’s rules, regulations & code of practice.

jobResponsibilities:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City

Develop World-Class Infrastructure

MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

The Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up in 2014 to improve the coordination, delivery and quality of municipal services by the Government and Town Councils.  These services include the upkeep and improvement of common areas in public and private housing estates, and the upgrading or provision of neighbourhood infrastructure.

jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for an experienced GIS professional to lead the standardisation and adoption of GIS solutions across LTA's engineering functions. In this role, you will work closely with engineering teams to understand their workflows, identify opportunities where GIS can add value, and develop reusable solutions that can be scaled across the organisation. You will also play a key outreach and enablement role — helping teams discover, adopt, and get the most out of GIS capabilities.

Your key responsibilities include:

  • Developing a thorough understanding of engineering workflows and processes across the organisation, building a clear picture of functional needs and priority pain points.
  • Defining and maintaining a structured framework of GIS use cases organised by common workflows, user groups, and data needs — mapping existing solutions against this framework to identify gaps, duplication, and opportunities for standardisation.
  • Designing and maintaining reusable GIS templates and solution frameworks, including for areas not yet served by existing tools, and assessing enterprise systems and platforms to ensure GIS solutions are fit for purpose.
  • Creating clear, task-based user guides and quick-start materials to help non-expert users get up and running with reusable templates.
  • Planning and leading outreach initiatives across Groups to showcase GIS capabilities, gather feedback, and drive uptake — including facilitating workshops and clinics to support users, address technical queries, and foster knowledge sharing.
  • Continuously scanning for opportunities to broaden the application of GIS across the organisation, translating these into proposed pilots, standards, or roadmap items.
jobRequirements:
• At least 10 years of experience in GIS, geospatial solutions, or related fields, with a demonstrated track record of delivering solutions for engineering, infrastructure, utilities, or asset management contexts.
  • Strong ability to elicit requirements from users, understand end-to-end workflows, and translate them into practical, scalable solutions — from prototype through to full rollout.
  • Hands-on experience creating reusable GIS assets such as templates, data models, map and app patterns, symbology standards, and reference architectures.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise applications and data platforms — such as EAM/CMMS, document management systems, BIM/CAD tools, and data lakes — and how GIS integrates with them.
  • Ability to produce clear, accessible documentation for diverse audiences including engineers, planners, and operational teams.
  • Experience designing and delivering workshops, training, or enablement programmes to drive adoption and build user capability.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills, with the ability to facilitate alignment and influence outcomes across teams without relying on formal authority.
  • A proactive and strategic mindset — with the ability to spot opportunities, prioritise value, and drive continuous improvement through well-designed standards and reusable solutions.

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and /or undergo further assessment.

ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Data Analysts work closely with economists, research analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate data-driven insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Data Analyst in ED, you will help to shape manpower policies in Singapore through the application of data science, advanced analytics and clear policy communication.

You will use a range of data analytics techniques – including machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling, statistical analysis, data visualisation and other frontier data science approaches – to examine traditional and emerging issues relating to manpower policies and the labour market.

Your work will contribute to strengthening the evidence base for policymaking, uncovering new insights from complex datasets, and supporting better outcomes for workers, businesses and Singapore’s labour market.
Your responsibilities will include:

•	Applying advanced analytics to manpower policy issues
Use data science techniques to analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, skills mismatches, job transitions, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Developing new analytical approaches and datasets
Identify, process and analyse novel datasets, including structured and unstructured data, to generate new insights on labour market trends, policy issues and operational challenges.

•	Using frontier data science methods
Apply methods such as machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling and simulation techniques to support policy analysis and decision-making.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and policy monitoring
Develop indicators, dashboards and analytical tools to monitor labour market developments, workforce trends and emerging risks in a timely and policy-relevant manner.

•	Strengthening policy design and operational effectiveness
Work with policymakers and operational divisions to translate data insights into practical recommendations that improve policy design, programme implementation and operational outcomes.

•	Collaborating with economists and researchers
Work closely with economists, research analysts and external partners to combine data science techniques with economic theory, empirical research and policy domain knowledge.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex analytical findings into clear, intuitive and policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who are intellectually curious, analytically rigorous and passionate about using data science to improve public policy.

You should have:
•	A degree, Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, Public Policy, or another quantitative discipline.
•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to frame policy problems and translate them into data analytics projects.
•	Strong quantitative and technical skills, including experience in statistical analysis, machine learning, predictive modelling, text analytics, network analytics and/or data visualisation.
•	Proficiency in programming and data analytics tools such as Python, R, SQL, Stata or other relevant software.
•	Experience handling large, complex datasets, including structured and/or unstructured data.
•	A strong interest in public policy, labour market issues and applied data science.
•	Good written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings clearly and logically to non-technical audiences.
•	The ability to work collaboratively with economists, researchers, policymakers, data specialists and operational teams.
•	A willingness to learn new methods, data sources and policy areas.

Candidates with experience in machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, causal inference, cloud-based analytics platforms, and/or dashboard development will have an advantage.

The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

jobDescription:
[What the role is]

You are the technical engine of our data exploration efforts. In the fast-paced world of tourism, new data opportunities emerge constantly, but their true value is often locked away. Your mission is to be the key that unlocks it.

This role is the technical counterpart to our Data Partnership Managers, forming a dynamic duo to accelerate our data pilots. While the Partnership Manager defines the business problem/opportunity and secures the data, you will deep-dive into the data - to wrangle the data, test hypotheses, and build compelling proof-of-concept dashboards and analyses. You are the "technical expert" in our "tech sales" model.

Success in this position means rapidly transforming raw, messy data from new data pilots and data partnerships into tangible, high-impact prototypes that showcase the possibilities and maximum potential we can achieve with our data. You will deliver the evidence and initial insights that determine which data pilots graduate to become scaled, industry-wide data products.

This contract role sits within the Data Exploration and Partnerships (DXP) department. We are looking for a data practitioner who is passionate in data exploration, experimentation, and moving quickly to create tangible impact.

[What you will be working on]

Technical Design & Feasibility Assessment:

  • Partner with Data Partnership Managers in later-stage discussions with potential data partners to finalise the scope and specifications of data exchange.

  • Act as the technical expert, assessing the quality, structure, and feasibility of using STB’s and our partner's data.

  • Help translate business problems into specific, testable analytical questions.

Hands-on Data Analysis & Prototyping:

  • Take the lead on the entire technical pilot process: data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation of new and diverse datasets.

  • Perform advanced exploratory data analysis (EDA) using Python to uncover hidden patterns, correlations, and insights that go beyond basic reporting.

  • Apply statistical methods to test hypotheses with rigour and build simple predictive models where applicable.

  • Lead technical discovery and experimentation, defining your own hypotheses and analytical approaches to uncover the most valuable insights.

  • Design and build compelling, interactive proof-of-concept dashboards (using tools like AWS QuickSight) that answer business questions clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Insight Generation & Storytelling:

  • Synthesize complex analytical findings into clear, concise insights and recommendations.

  • Collaborate with the Data Partnership Manager to present pilot findings back to internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating the value of the data collaboration.

  • Where possible and relevant, stretch the data pilots to include predictive and prescriptive insight.

Knowledge Transfer & Scaling Preparation:

  • Meticulously document the data sources, cleaning logic, analytical methodologies, and code for successful pilots.

  • Create a "recipe book" for each successful pilot that enables a smooth handover to the Data & AI Product Manager for evaluation and potential productisation onto our core Data and Analytics platform, STAN.

[What we are looking for]

Technical and Analytics skills:

  • Trained in a quantitative field such as Data Analytics, Computer Science, Statistics, Engineering, or Economics.

  • At least 3 years of demonstrable, hands-on experience in exploratory data analysis, data ingestion, transformation (cleaning, aggregation), and data modeling using large, real-world datasets.

  • Strong proficiency in statistical programming (e.g., Python) and database scripting (SQL) is essential.

  • Proven ability to develop compelling data visualizations and dashboards. Experience with tools like AWS QuickSight is highly advantageous.

  • A portfolio of projects (e.g., via GitHub, a personal website, or a slide deck) showcasing your hands-on data analysis and coding work is required.

  • Collaborative Partner: A strong team player who sees yourself as the technical counterpart to our business-facing managers. You are comfortable owning your technical workstream end-to-end while working closely with others to achieve a shared goal.

  • Comfortable with Ambiguity: A self-starter who thrives in an environment where priorities evolve and the path isn't always clear. You can take a vague business problem and messy data, and proactively find a path forward without waiting for instructions.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

As part of the current phase of PST, ServiceSG aims to be on par with globally leading companies in our delivery of public services. A key transformation in the delivery of citizen services is to take a citizen-centric service journey approach to organising services in an integrated manner via a) a digital concierge via the LifeSG app, b) a physical concierge via an expanded network of Service Centres; and c) a central contact centre. It has built-in levers to allow swift scale up a hired workforce whenever needed, and is working to expand the pool of manpower it could tap on, by identifying, tagging and training a group of public officers from the service delivery job role, to prepare them for immediate mobilisation to handle calls during a national emergency.

jobResponsibilities:
[ SAFEGUARD THE NATION ]
As a HAS (ICA) Direct-Entry Sergeant, you are responsible for the implementation and enforcement of the laws, regulations and policies of the various work of the Department. Your duties and responsibilities include the screening of passports and passengers on arrival and departure, participation in operations against smugglers, investigations, and conducting of raids against illegal immigrants.
 
[ STARTING SALARY ]
Diploma holders (5 local polytechnics / NAFA / LASALLE) - $2,870 to $3,233
GCE ‘A’ Level holders (including pass in GP / KI), IB Diploma / NUS High School Diploma - $2,870 to $3,233
Higher Nitec, Nitec and GCE ‘O’ Level holders - $2,342 to $2,618
*Starting salary will vary according to assessment during interview, relevant work experience and completion of full-time National Service.
 
[ $30,000 SIGN-ON BONUS ]
Newly appointed Direct Entry Sergeant will receive a sign-on bonus of $30,000, with $12,000 paid upon signing on and $18,000 upon confirmation after a one-year probation.
 
[ RETENTION PAYOUTS ]
Attractive retention payouts of $5,000 paid every 4 years, up to a maximum of 28 years.
 
[ BENEFITS ]
•            14 - 18 days vacation leave
•            Medical & dental subsidies
•            Group Life insurance
•            Sponsorship for continuous education
•            Use of government holiday bungalows
•            Subsidies for sports and recreation activities
•            Performance and annual bonuses
•            Marriage / Child benefits
•            Birthday vouchers
 
[ TRAINING ]
You will undergo a 20-week non-residential ICA Basic Course (Sergeant) at the Home Team Academy, which will equip officers with the knowledge and skills to perform their duties. Officers will be required to don on designated training attires during their Basic Course, which will include approved attires for physical trainings.
Training includes:
•            Document examination & forgery detection
•            People, goods and vehicle screening
•            Profiling techniques
•            Law and legislation
•            Firearms training
•            Control and restraint techniques
•            Attachment at Checkpoints, Enforcement Division and Services Centres
•            Home Team Basic Course
 
[ JOB DEPLOYMENT ]
Upon graduation from training school, you will be placed under a posting framework designed to provide you with exposure to the different aspects of border security and identification functions. You will be deployed at Checkpoints to work on three shifts. You are also required to wear uniform while on duty.
 
- Foundational Posting
Your first posting will be at one of the Commands, i.e. Woodlands, Tuas or Coastal Command.
- Developmental Posting
After your foundation posting, you will be deployed to other Checkpoints or Divisions where you will be given opportunities to perform specialised functions such as profiling, participation in operations against smugglers, investigation and conducting of raids against illegal immigrants.

jobDescription:
The Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX) is a statutory board under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) which aims to pioneer innovation solutions and develop world class science and technology capabilities to transform and empower the Home Team in delivering safety and security for Singapore. 
 
The HTxAI Products team is committed to empower our Home Team Department (HTD)'s flagship projects through the seamless integration of AI technologies. From identifying opportunities to delivery, launch, and continuous enhancement, HTxAI aims to push boundaries and setting new standards in public safety. 
 
You will join the core team behind the Phoenix LLM – a family of Sovereign AI models trained right here in Singapore. We are an ambitious and dynamic team of Applied AI Scientists building state-of-the-art Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) from the ground up. More about our work: http://go.gov.sg/phoenix-launch and https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10391

In this role, you will have the unique opportunity to push the frontier of Sovereign AI while collaborating on joint Applied R&D projects with global AI labs. You will have access to large GPU clusters for distributed AI training.
jobResponsibilities:
You post-train our LLMs for the agentic era: training it for our custom agentic workflows to call tools, carry out multi-step tasks. You will own the whole loop in a selected post-training domain: the reinforcement learning (RL) environments and harnesses the model learns in, the sandboxes where its actions run safely, the training tasks and the checkers that score them, and the fine-tuning and RL runs themselves.

This is not a role building chatbots or applications on top of LLM APIs; your work forms the core agentic capabilities of our models. 

LLM Post Training:
•	Run SFT and multi-turn RL on our GPU cluster, tune training recipe, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting
•	Read agent transcripts to find where the model fails, and fix it through changes to environments, data, rewards or training recipes
•	Check with our product team that gains hold up in real use
•	Contribute to our technical reports and papers

Environments and harnesses:
•	Build and scale tool-use and use-case-driven environments for agentic RL training, including tool servers and the automatic checkers that score the model's work
•	Maintain the harnesses that run our models through agentic tasks and benchmarks, used for both training and evaluation
•	Build containerised sandboxes on our GPU cluster, and own their security. That means code review, access controls - and testing that nothing escapes
jobRequirements:
•	Minimally Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent experience
•	Hands-on experience fine-tuning or training LLMs (for example, SFT or RL) in PyTorch, through work, research, internships or your own projects
•	Strong Python, and comfortable working on Linux
•	Keen to learn and experiment in a fast-paced Applied AI R&D environment

Good to have:
•	Experience with RL for LLMs (for example, GRPO, PPO or DPO)
•	Experience building agent harnesses, RL environments, evaluation harnesses, coding agents or sandboxed code execution
•	Distributed training experience on GPU clusters
•	Published papers or open source contributions

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every point above. Applicants with 5 or more years of relevant experience will be considered for senior roles.
