We are modernising the systems that ingest, manage, and make this data available for forecasting, climate analysis, and downstream services.

We are seeking a Staff Data Engineer to lead the technical design, delivery, and evolution of MSS’s Weather Data Lake.

You will help establish a governed, trusted foundation for meteorological and climate data. Working closely with MSS domain specialists and engineering teams, you will translate complex requirements into reliable data pipelines, clear architectural decisions, and maintainable platform capabilities.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role spanning data engineering, software engineering, and cloud infrastructure. You will set technical direction, lead critical implementation work, and strengthen engineering practices across the team. The platform runs on Microsoft Azure through Government on Commercial Cloud (GCC 2.0), using technologies including Databricks, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Apache Spark, and Terraform.

[What you will be working on]

Lead platform architecture and technical direction

  • Set the technical direction for MSS’s Weather Data Lake, balancing data processing, storage, security, governance, reliability, and cost.
  • Work with domain specialists and engineering teams to translate meteorological and climate data requirements into technical designs and delivery plans.
  • Define clear boundaries and interfaces between ingestion systems, the data lake, and downstream services, ensuring critical operational workflows do not depend directly on the availability of the analytical platform.
  • Document architectural decisions and build alignment on technical priorities, dependencies, and trade-offs.

Build reliable data pipelines and quality controls

  • Design, build, and optimise batch and streaming pipelines for meteorological observations, operational data, and international data exchanges.
  • Establish consistent approaches to data validation, schema evolution, incremental processing, reprocessing, and traceability.
  • Develop data quality approaches for operational forecasting and historical climate analysis, with appropriate controls for timeliness, validation, and the handling and propagation of corrections.
  • Lead historical data migration, including validation, reconciliation, cutover planning, and integration with downstream consumers.

Establish secure and maintainable platform foundations

  • Manage Databricks workspaces, storage, networking, and access controls through modular, version-controlled Terraform.
  • Establish CI/CD and environment-management practices for repeatable deployments, clear separation between staging and production, and controlled changes.
  • Implement data governance using Unity Catalog and supporting platform controls, including access policies, classification metadata, audit logging, and data lineage, in line with applicable IM8 and NEA requirements.
  • Evaluate platform capabilities against user needs, security requirements, operational readiness, and long-term cost and maintainability.

Grow engineering capability

  • Remain hands-on in complex engineering work while guiding technical design and implementation across the team.
  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, code reviews, pairing, and collaborative problem-solving.
  • Establish shared practices and documentation that make the platform easier to build, operate, and extend.
  • Help engineers develop the technical judgement and context to own platform capabilities independently.

  • A track record of leading complex technical initiatives, combining architectural ownership with hands-on delivery and collaboration across engineers or teams.
  • Strong hands-on experience building and operating production workloads on Databricks, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and Spark-based data processing.
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience developing and optimising large-scale batch or streaming pipelines using Spark.

  • Experience implementing data quality controls, governance, and lineage in production systems.

  • A track record of developing other engineers through mentoring, constructive feedback, and shared engineering practices.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work closely with domain specialists to understand unfamiliar data and workflows.

TradeNet is Singapore's National Single Window for trade permit processing. It handles over 9 million permit applications annually and accounts for around 10% of national tax revenues. We are replacing the decades-old legacy system with a modern, cloud-native platform.

The database work is the sharp end of this programme. Years of permit history, reference data, and business rules sit in legacy tables and stored procedures that were never fully documented. All of it has to move — correctly, provably, and without an outage window that agencies or traders would notice. Once it has moved, it has to hold up under sustained volume with clearing deadlines that don't wait for a slow query.

You are the person the programme relies on for this. You own the migration approach, the operational health of the estate, and the standards squads follow when they touch data.

Teams here use AI-assisted development workflows daily, including LLM/agentic-AI tooling for spec building, code generation, and test automation. You are expected to push the boundaries of what's possible with these tools.

[What you will be working on]

Legacy Data Migration

  • Own the migration of legacy production data end to end: extraction, transformation, loading, reconciliation, and cutover. You write and run the scripts, not only the plan.

  • Build the reconciliation tooling that proves the migrated data is correct — row counts, financial sums, referential integrity, and business invariants checked on both sides.

  • Design and execute phased cutovers using dual-write, backfill, and shadow-read approaches, with a rollback path you have rehearsed.

  • Work out what legacy data means before you move it, by reading stored procedures, triggers, constraints, and the table relationships nobody wrote down.

  • Execute complex phased cutovers using a 'Co-existence' model for user cohorts, prioritizing batch-based migration over integrated strangler patterns to minimize legacy dependency risks.

  • Perform detective work to reverse-engineer undocumented business logic from legacy Oracle stored procedures and triggers before migration.

Performance and Tuning

  • Find and fix slow queries. Read execution plans, correct the bad ones, and tell the owning squad what to do differently next time.

  • Own indexing across the estate: add what's needed, remove what isn't, and watch the write cost.

  • Tune instance and server configuration — memory, work_mem, checkpoints, autovacuum, parallelism, connection limits.

  • Diagnose contention under production load: lock waits, long-running and idle-in-transaction connections, deadlocks, hot rows.

  • Own connection pooling and pool sizing, table and index bloat, vacuum strategy, and partitioning of large history tables.

  • Do capacity planning and cost tuning. Right-size instances and storage instead of scaling up by reflex.

Database Operations and Reliability

  • Own backup and recovery, including scheduled test restores and point-in-time recovery. Verifying that backups ran is not the same as knowing you can restore.

  • Own high availability and disaster recovery: streaming replication, read-replica routing, lag monitoring, and failover drills you actually execute.

  • Plan and run major and minor version upgrades with minimal downtime.

  • Build observability for the data layer so problems surface before users report them — slow queries, replication lag, bloat and vacuum health, pool saturation.

  • Take part in on-call for database incidents, lead root-cause analysis, and publish the written follow-up.

Schema, security, and governance

  • Review and approve schema changes and migrations from squads before they reach production, especially on shared and high-volume tables.

  • Run schema change safely against live traffic: online index builds, non-blocking DDL, throttled backfills, expand-contract patterns for column changes.

  • Own access control and least-privilege roles across environments, encryption at rest and in transit, credential rotation, and secrets handling.

  • Implement data classification, masking, and anonymisation for non-production environments.

Technical leadership (without headcount)

  • Set the programme's standards for migration safety, schema change, performance, and operational hygiene, and build the tooling that makes those standards easy to follow.

  • Make the trade-off between data integrity and delivery timelines explicit and visible. Some shortcuts are acceptable; some data damage cannot be undone, and you are the one who says so.

  • Advise application engineers on transaction boundaries, isolation levels, idempotency, retry behaviour, and ORM patterns that generate poor SQL.

[What we are looking for]

  • At least 9 years of hands-on database engineering or DBA experience on production systems with real transaction volume and real consequences for downtime.

  • Deep Oracle expertise: query tuning and execution plans, indexing, partitioning, vacuum and bloat management, replication, connection pooling, configuration tuning.

  • Experience with PostgreSQL as a target architecture, including schema transformation, PL/pgSQL conversion, and heterogeneous replication (Oracle to Postgres).

  • A track record migrating large production datasets off legacy platforms, including reconciliation, phased cutover, and rollback planning where losing data is not an acceptable outcome. You've done this before and know where it goes wrong.

  • Strong operational depth: backup and recovery with tested restores and PITR, high availability, failover, monitoring, and incident response as first responder.

  • Ability to reconstruct business logic from legacy database artefacts: stored procedures, triggers, constraints, undocumented relationships.

  • Strong SQL, plus comfort with application code and ORMs to debug across.

  • Experience with CDC and replication tooling such as Golden Gate, AWS DMS, or logical replication.

  • Experience running databases on AWS (RDS, Aurora).

  • Scripting ability for automation in Python, Bash, or similar.

  • Practical experience with database security and compliance controls: roles and privileges, encryption, masking, audit logging.

  • Strong written technical communication. Your migration plans, runbooks, and incident write-ups need to stand on their own and be executable without you in the room.

  • Background in trade, customs, regulatory, or financial platform engineering.

As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

A hands-on Staff Software Engineer who will provide technical and technical-product leadership for GovTech's workflow automation platform product, with a particular focus on shaping
and leading a new operational data-layer capability within the platform.

[What you will be working on]

As a Staff Software Engineer in the Transaction Platforms Programme (TPP), you will play a key technical leadership role in shaping and building GovTech’s workflow automation platform product.


The platform product enables government agencies to automate workflows, orchestrate agents, define business rules, and integrate with Whole-of-Government tools. As part of TPP’s broader vision, this platform product works alongside other platform capabilities that agencies can compose to build and deliver digital services.


We are exploring a new capability within this ecosystem to address a key gap: the operational data layer. This is still in its early stages, and you will have the opportunity to shape the solution from the ground up - from understanding the problem and validating product-market fit, to defining its boundaries, architecture, and how it fits cohesively within the platform product and the wider TPP ecosystem.


This is not purely an architecture or delivery role. We are looking for someone who brings strong product thinking alongside deep technical expertise. You will work closely with Product to understand users and the market, evaluate approaches and trade-offs, prototype ideas, and translate these insights into technical product direction.


You will provide technical leadership to the team while remaining hands-on—designing systems, writing and reviewing code, establishing engineering practices, and solving difficult problems around scalability, performance, resilience, and distributed systems.


As we build new capabilities, you will also help us think AI-native from the outset: identifying how agentic and AI capabilities change the way we design the product, its architecture, and the experiences we offer our users.


As a Staff Engineer, your impact will extend beyond a single module or team. You will collaborate with other Staff Engineers, Engineering Managers, Product Managers, and engineers across TPP to ensure that the capabilities we build form a coherent, scalable, and well-architected platform for government.

[What we are looking for]

You should have:

  • Substantial hands-on experience in workflow automation, orchestration, integration platforms, data infrastructure, or closely related product domains. We value experience that gives you a deep understanding of how these systems behave in real-world use, including their constraints, failure modes, and product trade-offs.

  • A strong track record of contributing to product direction, not only technical implementation. You have helped identify what should be built, shaped product capabilities and boundaries, evaluated alternatives, and turned ambiguous problems into solutions that deliver meaningful user value.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills, including experience designing complex systems comprising multiple services and components.

  • Deep understanding of distributed systems and practical experience solving problems involving scalability, performance, resilience, reliability, and failure handling.

  • Strong technical judgement and the ability to reason through unfamiliar or ambiguous problems, identify the important trade-offs, challenge assumptions, and arrive at pragmatic decisions.

  • Experience leading technical direction and execution while remaining hands-on with software development.

  • A track record of raising engineering quality through technical practices, architecture, design and code reviews, mentoring, and improving how teams deliver software.

  • The ability to work effectively across Engineering and Product, connecting user and product needs with technical possibilities and constraints.

  • Experience or strong familiarity with AI-native and agentic systems, and the ability to reason about how these capabilities should influence product and system architecture.

  • Experience building workflow engines, orchestration systems, integration platforms, developer platforms, or operational data infrastructure at scale would be particularly relevant.

[What you will be working on]

Reporting to the Deputy Director for Smart City (Policy & Products Strategy), you will be part of a specialized technical policy triad responsible for shaping Whole-of-Government (WOG) smart city infrastructure. While your peers focus on Operational Technology (OT) Cybersecurity and Service Journey/Middleware architecture, your mandate is outward-looking cross-sector integration. Leveraging the INCOSE Systems Engineering lifecycle, you will partner with diverse government agencies to study their unique sectoral requirements, uncover systemic interoperability gaps, and formulate strategic policies to prevent cross-agency integration failures. You will act as the strategic bridge, ensuring that our overarching smart city policies and product strategies perfectly align with on-the-ground sectoral realities.

What You'll Do

  • Sectoral Needs Discovery & Roadmapping: Engage with cross-sector government agencies (e.g., transport, energy, environment) to study their cyber-physical ecosystems. Identify macro-level interoperability gaps and determine where the WOG needs to strategize and focus its integration efforts.

  • Triad Collaboration & Strategic Alignment: Work hand-in-hand with the OT Cybersecurity and OT Policy & Service Journey systems engineers. Ensure that the sectoral requirements you discover directly inform WOG security frameworks, smart city middleware architecture, and strategic procurement specifications.

  • Policy Formulation & Governance: Develop the strategic guidelines and governance frameworks that address the root causes of systemic integration failures. Establish the "rules of the road" for how disparate physical and digital systems must connect and share data across agency boundaries.

  • Engineering Practice Normalization: Institutionalize standardized systems engineering processes across the public sector. Define the strategic blueprints and integration frameworks that normalize how government agencies procure, architect, and deploy connected System of Systems (SoS).

  • Stakeholder Alignment & Advisory: Act as a strategic advisor to agency leaders and technical directors. Facilitate cross-agency collaboration to ensure localized sectoral requirements align with the broader national smart city and cyber-physical product strategies.

[What we are looking for]

  • Professional Credentials: Degree in a related engineering field (e.g., Systems Engineering, Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering). INCOSE Certification, such as Associate Systems Engineering Professional (ASEP) or Certified Systems Engineering Professional (CSEP) preferred.

  • Minimum 4–6 years of experience, with a strong background in technology policy, enterprise architecture, strategic planning, or technical governance within OT/cyber-physical environments.

  • A solid engineering foundation coupled with the ability to step back and apply systems thinking at a macro, System of Systems (SoS) level.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management, negotiation, and communication skills. You must be able to translate complex engineering challenges into clear strategic priorities for agency leaders and your technical peers.

Advantage to have

  • Domain Expertise: Prior experience shaping policy for large-scale public infrastructure, smart city platforms, or multi-agency technological deployments.

  • Strategic Frameworks: Familiarity with enterprise architecture frameworks (e.g., TOGAF) or the macro-level application of systems engineering methodologies to guide organizational strategy.

The Government Digital Products (GDP) Team aims to spearhead the digital transformation of government. Our team designs and develops software applications that help government agencies to better serve the needs of the people of Singapore.
At the Engagement and Case Management Programme (ECMP), our products are the primary touchpoints through which residents interact with the Singapore Government. We design and develop a suite of high-impact software applications including FileSG, Signify, PersonaliseSG, CrowdTask SG, and BookingSG.

The Challenge: Elevating BookingSG

BookingSG is a comprehensive Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution designed to unify, simplify, and manage appointments and resource scheduling across Whole-of-Government (WOG) agencies. Far from a simple calendar app, BookingSG is a highly customizable, multi-tenant platform built on a versatile architecture featuring Calendaring, Availability, Rostering, and Booking (CARB) capabilities.

Trusted by 50+ government agencies across 60+ distinct use cases, our platform handles over 1.5 million transactions—and we are just getting started. Whether it's high-volume facility bookings or complex citizen appointment routing, our mission is to turn fragmented legacy systems into elegant, out-of-the-box digital booking experiences at a national scale.

We are looking for a Technical Lead / Engineering Manager to spearhead the next evolution of this platform. You will take full engineering ownership of a nimble, cross-functional squad — balancing enterprise architecture and high-velocity shipping with hands-on coaching to level up our engineering practices.

You will work closely with Product, Design, and Engineering partners to solve complex problems, deliver high-impact features, and continuously improve how the team builds and operates software.

[What you will be working on]

Lead and Nurture a High-Performing Squad.

  • Lead, mentor, and develop a cross-functional engineering team (comprising internal engineers, vendors, or external contributors) to deliver high-quality platform capabilities.
  • Provide pragmatic, hands-on technical guidance to unblock complex engineering bottlenecks while fostering autonomy.
  • Cultivate a culture of strong technical ownership and continuous improvement. Support engineers' career growth through regular coaching, actionable technical feedback, and modern engineering practices.

Drive Technical Strategy and Platform Evolution

  • Define and evolve the technical architecture of BookingSG, balancing short-term feature speed with long-term platform sustainability and enterprise scalability standards.
  • Evaluate and implement technical solutions that meet strict Whole-of-Government security and compliance standards.
  • Actively identify and mitigate technical risks, maintaining a healthy balance between shipping new product capabilities and reducing technical debt.
  • Partner with Product Managers, UX Designers, Infrastructure, and Platform teams to align on product roadmap execution, system dependencies, and cross-team technical initiatives.

Elevate Engineering & Operational Excellence

  • Champion best practices in system design, code quality, automated testing, and comprehensive code/architecture reviews.
  • Drive strong operational ownership. Champion robust CI/CD pipelines, containerization, infrastructure-as-code, and comprehensive test automation.
  • Utilize engineering and operational metrics (e.g., system reliability, performance, delivery flow) to continuously optimize team’s effectiveness and system stability.
  • Establish scalable engineering processes such as design reviews, architecture discussions, and effective code reviews.
  • Keep the platform cutting-edge. Guide the team in pragmatically evaluating and integrating GenAI for automated routing and intelligent administrative workflows.

[What we are looking for]

Experience

  • 5–7+ years of experience engineering, scaling, and delivering production-grade web applications, with a heavy emphasis on robust backend systems.
  • Demonstrated experience operating as a Technical Lead or Engineering Manager within an agile environment. Proven ability to align engineering squads and manage vendor deliverables or hybrid teams is a strong plus.
  • A solid track record of designing, architecting, and operating scalable distributed systems, ideally within multi-tenant SaaS platforms or enterprise-grade applications.

Technical Skills

  • Deep, production-tested expertise in Node.js and TypeScript / Go.
  • Strong hands-on experience building web applications and robust APIs using React or Next.js.
  • Solid understanding of cloud platforms (AWS preferred), container technologies (Docker), and establishing or operating modern CI/CD pipelines.
  • Deep commitment to comprehensive automated testing practices (unit, integration, and end-to-end) and structured architectural reviews.
  • Exposure to or a strong interest in GenAI technologies and incorporating AI-powered capabilities into product features is highly advantageous.

Leadership & Mindset

  • Strong technical judgment with the ability to make practical architectural trade-offs between rapid product innovation, system stability, and strict security guardrails.
  • An excellent communicator who can seamlessly translate complex technical challenges into clear business contexts for product, design, and agency stakeholders.
  • Passionate about mentoring talent, building psychological safety, and fostering a collaborative, high-velocity squad environment.
  • Highly analytical, detail-oriented, and inherently curious about optimizing both software architecture and team execution processes.

GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore's Smart Nation initiative and public sector digital transformation. We harness the power of technology to make lives better for citizens, businesses, international audiences and the public service sector.

Digital Economy Products (DEP) is a division within GovTech run like a modern product company, solving important underserved problems spanning across Healthcare, Manpower, Trade-Industry-Finance, National Development, and Sustainability sectors.

Designers at DEP are key to our success. They work closely with product managers, researchers, software engineers, and public sector stakeholders, bringing purposeful ideas to life with excellent visual and interaction design, skillfully shaping how users feel when using our services.

About the product

Through the GreenGov initiative, the government has committed to the public its aim to achieve net-zero emissions by approximately 2045. Furthermore, it has established clear and measurable milestones to facilitate progress across all agencies. Since the year 2021, agencies have utilised the eGreenGov portal, which is housed within the National Environment Agency’s Waste and Resource Management System (WRMS), to report various environmental data of their respective premises.

The Public Sector Sustainability Office (PSSO) reviews the progress of agencies, provides updates to the Cabinet, and produces the annual GreenGov report championing the GreenGov initiative. They intend to help agencies identify opportunities to improve resource efficiency and climate resilience, and partner them to streamline the process of implementing these improvements.

Responsibilities

  • Understand PSSO’s mission and users’ needs

  • Create mockups and intuitive user flows that drive climate action at scale

  • Test early designs with users; iterate with feedback

  • Create detailed user interface specifications

  • Guide engineers in implementing your designs

  • Execute overall aesthetics that align with branding and design principles

  • Help progressively build and adapt a design system, that scales and flexes across a variety of user groups for the product

As a designer on this product, you’ll also get to learn and experiment with green design practices, taking a truly systemic approach towards responsible design and tech for public good.

We’re looking for a designer with:

  • Demonstrated ability in interaction and visual design — ideally 5+ years of experience in digital design

  • Great visual design sense and eye for detail

  • User- and data-focused design mentality

  • Proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite

  • Experience building responsive and accessible designs

  • Communicate well with users and engineers

  • A “can-do” attitude

  • Want to work for public good — respectfully pushing back if something is not in the public’s interest, including that of the environment.

These will be a plus:

  • Experience creating a simple and elegant design system

  • Interest in continually growing your visual design craft

  • Strong belief and drive for sustainability is a plus!

Overall, we look for people who are collaborative, value open communications, and take initiative to improve things.

agencyDescription:
The Public Service Division (PSD) stewards a trusted Singapore Public Service for a successful and vibrant Singapore. Our 4 key roles include:

  • Developing a flourishing and diverse workforce by supporting our public officers' continual growth of skills and creating meaningful careers
  • Developing a forward-looking and inspiring community of leaders who are united, resilient, and anchored in public service values and ethos
  • Building future-ready public sector organisations by steering and supporting transformation of our organisations and catalysing innovations for organisations to work more effectively
  • Driving good governance, values and excellence to safeguard the integrity and reputation of the Public Service and uphold the trust of citizens

Why Join Us

When you join PSD, you become part of a community that learns together and cares for one another. We look out for your well-being and partner you in your career growth. Being in the business of developing People and driving transformation makes our work deeply Purposeful. What you do will impact our public officers and agencies, and in turn make a difference to Singapore and Singaporeans.

If you share our passion in reimagining Possibilities and pushing boundaries to shape a first-class Public Service, we welcome you to join us!

People, Our Pride | Service, Our Pledge | Integrity, Our Core | Excellence, Our Quest
jobDescription:
The Challenge

The Public Service operates in an increasingly complex environment shaped by changing citizen expectations, workforce shifts, technological disruption and greater interdependence across agencies. Public Sector Transformation (PST) seeks to ensure that the Singapore Public Service remains future-ready, effective and trusted by continually reimagining how the Public Service works, develops its workforce and organises itself.

The PST Cluster leads and coordinates Whole-of-Government transformation. Its role spans setting the vision and strategic direction for PST, catalysing deep organisational and business transformation, building the capabilities and ecosystem needed to sustain change, applying AI to the key challenges of today and mobilising leaders and officers around a shared transformation agenda.

As Assistant Director (Strategy), you will provide strategic and organisational leadership across key PST strategic portfolios, covering sensemaking, conceptualising, catalyst and mobilising workstreams. You will translate emerging priorities and senior leadership direction into coherent strategies, governance arrangements, programmes and resourcing approaches that enable transformation across the Public Service.

This is both a strategy and delivery role. You will work at the intersection of policy, organisational transformation, innovation, technology, workforce capability and public-sector governance, while leading teams to turn broad and often ambiguous ambitions into practical, coordinated action.

Key Responsibilities

As a Team Lead to a team of 3-5 officers, you will:

A. Set and steward the strategic direction for Public Sector Transformation

  • Lead the development and continual refinement of the overarching PST strategy, identifying the major shifts required for the Public Service to remain effective and future-ready.
  • Synthesise emerging operating-environment trends, ground sentiment, organisational data and agency experience to surface strategic priorities and areas requiring Whole-of-Government intervention.
  • Translate senior leadership direction into clear transformation outcomes, priorities, implementation pathways and narratives for agencies, leaders and officers.
  • Ensure PST priorities remain aligned with broader Whole-of-Government, Centre-of-Government and Public Service priorities.
  • Oversee the monitoring and reporting of PST progress, surfacing key achievements, implementation challenges and areas requiring leadership attention.

B. Lead cross-cutting and AI-enabled transformation

  • Shape and coordinate major cross-cutting transformation priorities requiring joint ownership across policy, technology, workforce and corporate-function stakeholders.
  • Provide strategic leadership for AI-enabled PST, ensuring technology adoption is connected to business and workflow redesign, organisational change, workforce implications and measurable outcomes.
  • Work with functional and mission leads to identify high-impact transformation opportunities, define the desired picture of success and establish coherent governance and tracking arrangements.
  • Develop proposals for the capabilities, funding, headcount and specialist support needed to implement transformation at scale.

C. Shape resourcing, governance and implementation arrangements

  • Design governance and operating arrangements that clarify accountability, enable timely decisions and provide progress assurance without imposing unnecessary process.
  • Develop and evaluate funding and manpower proposals for Whole-of-Government transformation initiatives, working with finance and policy partners to align transformation funding with strategic outcomes.
  • Establish portfolio-level measures, review mechanisms and reporting arrangements that support learning and course correction.

D. Mobilise and align Whole-of-Government partners

  • Build trusted relationships with Centre-of-Government partners, ministries, statutory boards, transformation offices and delivery agencies.
  • Convene stakeholders around shared outcomes, particularly where responsibilities and resources are distributed across organisations.
  • Develop engagement approaches across multiple levels, from senior leadership forums to working-level communities and agency visits.

E. Lead teams and manage an evolving portfolio

  • Review and assure the quality of key products, including strategies, submissions, briefs, programme designs and senior-leadership materials.
  • Build a collaborative, high-performing team culture that is comfortable with ambiguity, experimentation and constructive challenge.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for someone who is curious about the future of government, passionate about AI and innovation, and excited to work with diverse stakeholders to shape meaningful transformation across the Public Service.

You enjoy solving complex problems, thrive in collaborative environments and are motivated by turning ideas into practical impact. Whether developing AI-enabled initiatives, building partnerships or supporting innovation programmes, you are driven by a desire to improve outcomes for citizens and public officers alike.

Key Competencies

1. Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgement

o You consider stakeholder needs as well as short- and long-term implications in proposing solutions.

o You make sound judgements about different policy options by synthesising various data points and using a good sense of realities on the ground.

o You anticipate and prepare for queries from stakeholders when operationalising solutions.

o You guide your team to demonstrate care and empathy in delivering services to citizens and stakeholders.

o You are a role model of, and ensure that your team upholds, the Public Service values in the course of their work.

o You are a role model of resilience and bouncing back from adversity.

o You orchestrate resources and monitor your team’s progress towards deliverables.

The PST Cluster leads and coordinates Whole-of-Government transformation.   • Support the translation of senior leadership direction into clear transformation outcomes, priorities, implementation pathways and narratives for agencies, leaders and officers.
  • Ensure PST priorities remain aligned with broader Whole-of-Government, Centre-of-Government and Public Service priorities.

  • Shape and coordinate major cross-cutting transformation priorities requiring joint ownership across policy, technology, workforce and corporate-function stakeholders.

  • Develop proposals for the capabilities, funding, headcount and specialist support needed to implement transformation at scale.
